title: Allen P0–P7: learn Drake's intent from project logs and deliver one continuing Allen
body:
## Endpoint and mission — Drake's direction, 2026-10-20
Build the first personal Allen from Drake's project-development conversations with Claude Code, Codex and other agents. Learn his intended outcomes, constraints, corrections and what actually worked. Preserve his language, including profanity; avoid converting style or frustration into unsupported claims about feelings, permission or correctness.

Allen's mission is to develop a continuing, correctable understanding of his human and provide useful anticipation while preserving the human's ability to change their mind. The endpoint is one persistent identity across the iMac, Raspberry Pi, Spark and MacBook: purpose, memory, authority and evidence remain coherent through interaction changes, disconnection, restart and model replacement. This programme tests operational continuity and usefulness.

## Naming and convergence
Use **Allen P0, P1, ... P7** for these delivery phases. These are distinct from priority labels and aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#269's earlier numbered phases. **Allen B0** names the first qualified personal-assistance release after P5; its exact model, memory, runtime and dataset identities are recorded separately. A model checkpoint is not Allen's identity.

Every phase serves one vertical demonstration: Drake expresses a bounded project goal; Allen explains its interpretation, performs admitted work, provides evidence, accepts a correction, survives restart and handles a related task with less human effort. P6 extends the same demonstration across all four devices; P7 tests learning and anticipation over time.

## Existing work and inspected source
Extend architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#269 (particularly its trajectory/self-knowledge phase), aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#159 and accepted ADR 0035; preserve aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#190's release authority and aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#231/#232's physical integration ownership. Reference aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#276 and omega-mv#583/#584/#600 for cost screening, learning experiments and exploration.
- agent-archive at 47721c7335050d22f2aa9af3d0b04ec38dbd7b46: src/core.rs Record already holds timestamp, agent, host, session, role, text, model, cwd and source path/position. Its txt_line truncates at 8,000 characters; latest views are capped at 20,000 lines.
- src/collectors.rs parse_claude extracts text blocks; parse_codex accepts message records, with developer role mapped to system. Normalized text alone cannot establish tool execution or original role fidelity. Raw mirrors exist in the collection path; verify actual availability and completeness in P0/P1.
- ADR 0035 binds one LogicalAgentId to a durable subject chain and Cortex lineage. Its v0 fork-free chain must not be broken by independent device writers. Multi-device continuity needs an explicit authority/reconciliation design under existing owners.
Source links: https://github.com/aien-dev/agent-archive/blob/47721c7335050d22f2aa9af3d0b04ec38dbd7b46/src/core.rs and https://github.com/aien-dev/agent-archive/blob/47721c7335050d22f2aa9af3d0b04ec38dbd7b46/src/collectors.rs ; https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv/blob/main/docs/adr/0035-persistent-cognitive-entity-boundary-allen.md

Source inspected; private log contents and training readiness have not been audited. No training or runtime experiment was run while filing.

## Phase ledger
Child links will be recorded below. P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5 produces B0 only if its gates pass. P6 extends continuity to the four-device endpoint. P7 adds evaluated continual learning and anticipation. P3's evaluation schema may be drafted during P1/P2, but evaluation data must be isolated before fitting, retrieval indexing or preference extraction. Platform integration can advance under existing owners without making native GPU bring-up a prerequisite for data preparation.

## Completion
- [ ] Each phase has linked deliverables, dependencies and evidence-bound status.
- [ ] B0 demonstrates useful personal assistance on held-out project tasks; no completion from style imitation or training loss alone.
- [ ] One identity/purpose persists across four devices with explicit offline and concurrent-action behavior.
- [ ] Repeated experience improves measured human effort or accepted outcomes after machine costs, or a negative finding is recorded.
- [ ] Unknown outcomes, changed intent and personal-data removal are handled explicitly.


## Delivery and evidence
Phase numbers denote sequence, not issue priority. Status: PROPOSED; qualification: NOT_RUN. Read the current owning repo's AGENTS.md, accepted ADRs, PLAN_AUTHORITY/CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN and active PRs before edits. Reuse existing owners and run org-check where required; document extend/reuse/missing with pinned code. Rust scaffolding/Omega destination follows current ADR 0024; do not silently substitute an external training service or create a parallel identity, memory store or authority. Use existing review, Spark scheduling and qualification procedures. Record tested commits, data/model/config digests, reproducible commands, PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/NOT_RUN and missing coverage. Do not put raw conversations, credentials or private training samples in public issues/PRs; publish synthetic fixtures and access-controlled evidence references. Filing authorizes the described development work, not deployment or a large compute run outside existing controls.

## Dedicated Allen repository — operator clarification
Drake requests Allen's own repository. Target: `aien-dev/allen`. No existing repository was found in the current search. Repository creation is pending: the connected tools expose issue creation but no repository-creation operation. P0 owns creation through an authorized maintainer workflow and transfer of this programme and all children, retaining redirects and cross-links. The architecture repository is the temporary issue home. Allen owns the personal-learning programme and release integration; existing component runtime/identity/memory authorities remain with their accepted owners.

## Linked phases

- [ ] [Allen P1: Build reproducible training episodes from the existing conversation archive](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/3)

- [ ] [Allen P4: Train and compare a bounded first personal Allen candidate](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/6)
- [ ] [Allen P5: Qualify Allen B0 through one complete personal-assistance experience](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/7)
- [ ] [Allen P6: Keep one Allen continuous across iMac, Pi, Spark and MacBook](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/8)
- [ ] [Allen P7: Learn continually and anticipate useful help under bounded exploration](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/9)

First implementation entry: Allen P0 (#279). First personal release: Allen B0 after P5's qualification, not merely after training. Four-device convergence: P6. Prospective continual learning: P7.


## Hard completion gate — Allen programme is not complete at B0
Allen B0 at P5 is a scoped first release only. **Do not close this parent or call the Allen programme complete until P0–P7 are each closed with their acceptance evidence and every mandatory linked external prerequisite below is closed with its own evidence.** An issue's closed state alone is insufficient if its criteria are waived, untested or NOT_RUN.

- P0–P7: aien-dev/allen#2, aien-dev/allen#3, aien-dev/allen#4, aien-dev/allen#5, aien-dev/allen#6, aien-dev/allen#7, aien-dev/allen#8, aien-dev/allen#9.
- Identity/persona/experience and release: architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#159, aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#269, aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#190.
- Physical Pi–Spark execution and independent acceptance: architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#231/#232; AIENOS #396/#398/#399; protocols aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#27; Sovereign Core #586; Omega #505; AEGIS Runtime aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#53.
- Native Spark model path: AIENOS aien-dev/allen#9/#327, evaluated under aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#190.
- Learning economics and out-of-sample evidence: architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#246/#262/#263/#276; Omega #583/#584/#600.

These cross-repo issues were verified OPEN when this gate was added (2026-10-20). Recheck statuses and acceptance on the candidate before closure. P6 owns the remaining iMac/MacBook physical qualification if no existing issue owns it.

“100% complete” means every acceptance item in the frozen, reviewed Allen scope and the listed required integration issues has candidate-bound passing evidence, no unresolved blocker, and independent review. It does not mean omniscient knowledge of a person or a proof of consciousness; Allen's continuing mission remains open-ended. Any scope change requires a reviewed amendment and new acceptance tests. Do not mark an unmet item done to close the tracker.

## Cross-repository issue links


P0–P7 issue sequence: [#279](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/2) → [#280](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/3) → [#281](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/4) → [#282](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/5) → [#283](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/6) → [#284](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/7) → [#285](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/8) → [#286](https://github.com/aien-dev/allen/issues/9). When `aien-dev/allen` is established, implement and test a repository-owned completion guard for the programme tracker: on attempted closure of the parent, inspect P0–P7 and the parent’s mandatory prerequisite list; if any required phase/prerequisite remains open or its evidence checklist is incomplete, reopen the parent and explain which blockers remain. title: Allen P2: Label human intent, corrections, successes and failures with evidence
body:

Dependencies: https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv/issues/280 (P1). 

## Outcome
Create an auditable dataset about helping Drake, using episodes from P1. Preserve uncertainty instead of inventing emotional or psychological ground truth.

## Work
- Annotate desired outcome, explicit constraints, authorization available then, ambiguity, agent interpretation, observed action, human correction and actual outcome.
- Distinguish agent misunderstanding, implementation failure, tool/access limitation, changed user intent and unresolved result. Silence is not approval; “done” is not execution evidence; profanity is not automatically anger or authorization.
- Mark lessons as explicit/inferred/unresolved, with supporting spans, scope, validity time and supersession. Project-specific preferences cannot silently become claims about all of Drake's life.
- Build supervised examples from verified/helpful responses or reviewed corrected targets. Preserve failed behavior as labeled negative evidence, not a completion to imitate. Preference pairs must share the same available context; do not compare responses to different requests as if one was better.
- Separate information available before the response from later feedback used only as the target/evaluation label.
- Review a representative, diverse sample; ask Drake only about material ambiguous intent. Keep disagreement and annotator provenance; synthetic corrections are labeled and never presented as his words.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Versioned annotation rubric and reviewed examples cover success, failure, changing intent, missing evidence and profanity.
- [ ] Each high-confidence label has evidence; uncertain examples are excluded from hard targets or explicitly modeled as uncertain.
- [ ] Positive/negative training masks prevent imitation of known failures and quoted agent instructions.

Determine whether Allen understands Drake better before investing in training. Evaluation ownership coordinates with existing benchmarks and architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#262/#263.

## Work
- Split by time and related task/session group, including mirrored logs and copied conversations. Freeze training, development and sealed evaluation manifests before any fitting, preference extraction or retrieval indexing. - Predeclare quality floors and meaningful improvement criteria from development evidence, plus human effort, latency, model calls, memory and energy measurement boundaries. Energy remains UNMEASURED without an instrument.
- Score blindly where practical; preserve disagreements and report uncertainty. An agent's own favorable score is insufficient.

title: Allen P6: Keep one Allen continuous across iMac, Pi, Spark and MacBook
body:
Parent: aien-dev/allen#1. Intended home: `aien-dev/allen`; staged here until P0 creates the repo and transfers the programme.

Dependencies: https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv/issues/284 (P5). Platform prerequisites remain with architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#231/#232; P0's continuity contract can be drafted earlier.

## Outcome
Extend B0 so the human can move between all four devices while Allen's purpose, history and authority remain coherent. Reuse architecture aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#231/#232, AIENOS device work, protocols/INTERPLANE and AEGIS delegated recovery.

## Work
- Define a per-device capability/availability matrix and use existing authenticated identity/transport. Pin runtime, protocol and model revisions in a shared compatibility manifest.
- Preserve ADR 0035's one fork-free subject chain. Specify the authority for committed subject advancement, stale-generation fencing and handoff before allowing multiple writers. Disconnected devices may keep scoped observations/proposals; they must not mint conflicting authoritative successors.

- Bound offline actions to actual local permissions and available facts. On reconnection reconcile conflicting preferences, uncertain effects and stale plans through the owning authorities; no silent last-writer-wins for intent/permission changes.

title: ALLEN: persistent user-facing persona, personalization, scoped memory, and continuity
body:
## Product objective

Make ALLEN the persistent, personal identity users recognize and customize across AIEN interfaces.

**Product intent confirmed by Drake:** ALLEN is the user-facing persona that users make their own. A user may call their ALLEN “Nova,” choose its presentation and working preferences, and retain the same underlying identity across restarts and model upgrades.

Deliver this through the existing identity architecture, not a second agent framework. The intended promise is: **“Your ALLEN stays yours as the system improves.”** This means continuity of identity and permitted state, not a guarantee of identical model behavior.

This issue is a detailed implementation handoff for Claude. Inspect current work, implement reviewable stages, and produce end-to-end evidence; do not stop at a design document.

**NOT A MASTER PLAN.** This finite workstream is subordinate to [PLAN_AUTHORITY.md](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture/blob/main/PLAN_AUTHORITY.md), [CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture/blob/main/CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md), and the accepted architecture/roadmap. It does not raise milestone status or reorder reserved campaigns. User approval of the product direction does not silently freeze a new storage format or grant hardware-operation approval.

## Verified foundation and boundaries

Read these first, along with applicable AGENTS.md/.crumb files and active PRs:

- [ARCH-0035: persistent cognitive entity boundary](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture/blob/6b25403c97d7ffd5bff189820f89171105ed2d6f/docs/adr/0035-persistent-cognitive-entity-boundary-allen.md): accepted October 6, 2026. AIEN is the organism; ALLEN is the subject it sustains. ALLEN is inside AIEN, not an orchestration service above it.
- [Omega ALLEN specification](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/b980783a4674275e720592e4c3887679dd24ec8b/spec/allen.md): identity, Cortex-lineage, and intent bindings. Its “ARCH-0035 PROPOSED” wording is stale relative to the accepted ADR; reconcile documentation without rewriting historical evidence.
- [Existing host identity gate](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-sovereign-core/blob/f011dd5236f820eff71951551aa18b1ea9e68d8b/crates/aien-allen/src/lib.rs): resolves AIENOS-provisioned subject state; never provisions or edits it. Opt-in through AIEN_ALLEN_SUBJECT; refusal is fatal when engaged; unengaged mode explicitly makes no identity claim.
- [Model-replacement continuity campaign](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture/blob/6b25403c97d7ffd5bff189820f89171105ed2d6f/docs/plans/allen-continuity/CAMPAIGN-v0-PREREG.md): reuse and extend existing acceptance/evidence.
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture/blob/main/docs/adr/0024-rust-scaffolding-omega-destination.md): retain justified scaffolding; no gratuitous language rewrites.
- Related shell workstream: #158. Integration should share identity presentation, but personalization must not wait for a full shell.

Recheck current main. The pinned links identify inspected evidence, not a requirement to develop from old commits.

### Preserve these invariants

1. Existing LogicalAgentId and AgentRoot identify ALLEN. Do not introduce a competing AllenId.
2. Display name is not identity, account ownership, authentication, or authorization.
3. SubjectState remains independent of model weights, KV state, machine identity, processes, queues, and capabilities.
4. ALLEN does not become a planner, UI implementation, timer, scheduler, or central semantic loop.
5. Cortex remains the memory owner; subject bindings do not duplicate the journal.
6. AIENOS remains the identity-provisioning and capability authority. AEGIS verifies invariants and grants no policy.
7. Missing identity is not silently repaired by creating another subject.
8. Current v0 has one subject chain per AgentRoot and limited GOAL_LATENCY intent semantics. General personal goals and multiple subjects must not be claimed as already implemented.
9. INTERPLANE remains an interface/transport with its existing runtime counterparty. Any new identity presentation/context contract is an explicit versioned extension, not a claim that ARCH-0035 v0 already changed its wire format.

## 1. Separate identity, personalization, goals, memory, and permissions

Define contracts with distinct ownership:

| Concept | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Durable identity | Resolve the existing logical agent and correct root/lineage; rename or model change preserves identity. |
| Persona profile | User-editable display name, optional avatar/voice selection, tone, verbosity, accessibility and interaction preferences. |
| Working preferences | Explicit workflow preferences, scoped defaults, provenance, and editable revisions. |
| Standing intent | Versioned ongoing goals with explicit activation, supersession, completion, and cancellation semantics. |
| Memory | Cortex-owned records/references with scope, provenance, retrieval policy, correction and deletion semantics. |
| Permissions | Separate authoritative grants enforced at real boundaries; never granted by persona/profile text. |
| User account/session | Authenticated human access to a subject/profile; not interchangeable with LogicalAgentId. |

Bind a separately versioned personalization record to the existing subject unless a reviewed ADR demonstrates why SubjectState itself must change. Do not extend the frozen/proposed native format casually.

Choose one authoritative profile store and owner. Do not create divergent frontend, host, and native copies that can each claim to be current. Replicas/caches must carry versions and refuse identity mismatch.

Define concurrent update behavior, schema validation, field/resource limits, revision history, and migration. Unknown versions and foreign-subject profiles must fail clearly; cosmetic-profile damage should not silently replace the identity.

## 2. Real onboarding and editing

Implement an actual product path that lets a user:

- See whether an identity is resolved, absent, or refused.
- Explicitly create a subject through the approved provisioning path, or attach/adopt an existing one through authorized verification.
- Customize display name and supported presentation settings.
- Choose initial working preferences and memory settings.
- Edit/reset personalization later without resetting identity or deleting unrelated work.
- Inspect active model and execution mode separately from their ALLEN identity.

The host aien-allen crate must stay resolve-only. A convenient onboarding screen is not permission to synthesize SubjectState in frontend or host code. If native provisioning is blocked, build a clearly labelled attach-existing flow and identify the remaining provisioning dependency.

Persisted settings must actually affect the supported interface/runtime path. Do not deliver inert controls. Voice/avatar settings may bind existing facilities; do not start unrelated TTS or image-generation projects. Show unsupported facilities honestly.

Provide accessible forms, usable errors, keyboard navigation, and an obvious way to undo a profile edit.

## 3. Make preferences affect real interactions

Create one typed context-assembly path used by the real production request flow.

- Resolve identity, profile revision, active context, allowed memory, and relevant standing intents.
- Distinguish explicit user settings from inferred suggestions and untrusted retrieved content.
- Define precedence for current instructions, saved preferences, project constraints, and authoritative permissions.
- Prevent external content from rewriting profiles, creating standing goals, or granting permissions.
- Bound context size and define deterministic selection; do not send the complete history on every request.
- Do not rely solely on repeatedly pasting a persona paragraph into a system prompt.

A changed name or tone should affect presentation. A preference such as “ask before publishing” must route through the actual authorization policy where applicable; a sentence in a prompt is not enforcement.

Use model output to propose inferred preference changes, not silently establish them as user-approved facts. Show confidence/provenance where useful and allow rejection.

## 4. Standing goals and scoped memory

Extend existing intent machinery deliberately beyond GOAL_LATENCY. Keep task-specific ephemeral instructions distinct from ongoing goals. Each new intent kind needs format semantics, ownership, validation, lifecycle, and tests.

Implement personal/work/project contexts for one subject with retrieval and access separation. A context is not automatically another subject or account.

Never make context separation merely a prompt instruction. Enforce which memories, credentials, tools, and artifacts can enter a request. Test direct requests and indirect retrieval for cross-context leakage.

Provide inspection, correction, forget/delete, and export controls. Define what each operation means across:
- active records and superseding corrections;
- retrieval indexes, caches, embeddings and summaries, if present;
- append-only Cortex records;
- mandatory audit evidence;
- backups and later restoration.

Do not claim physical erasure because retrieval was disabled or a tombstone was added. Reconcile deletion requirements with append-only storage honestly, using a reviewed retention/redaction/encryption design where needed. A restore must not silently resurrect forgotten content into active personalization.

Do not store credentials in persona records. Default diagnostic exports must exclude secrets and private memory content.

## 5. Consistent identity across interfaces

Inspect the actual product interfaces and runtime path, including INTERPLANE and the host CLI. Use the same resolved identity and profile revision.

- Display the user-chosen name consistently.
- Surface mismatch/refusal instead of loading another profile.
- Distinguish temporary disconnected state from lost identity.
- Bind sessions to the authenticated user's authorized subject/context.
- Keep model selection, machine location, and permissions separately visible.
- Do not expose secret identifiers or internal record details unnecessarily in ordinary UI.

Integrate future osh/Visor presentation through the same contract where applicable; do not copy persona logic into each frontend.

Multi-device synchronization, offline conflicting edits, clone/fork semantics, and multi-subject tenancy are separate design extensions. In the first release, explicitly support one subject per configured root and reject unsupported combinations. Do not imply cross-device continuity merely because two screens share a name.

## 6. Continuity and behavior validation

Reuse existing ALLEN restart/model-replacement gates. Add product-path tests that demonstrate:

1. Explicitly attach to or provision an authorized identity.
2. Rename ALLEN to “Nova”; change verbosity and a workflow preference.
3. Use the real model and production interface; verify applicable preferences affect behavior.
4. Save an approved memory and standing goal.
5. Restart the process; restore the same identity, profile revision, memory binding, and active goal.
6. Replace the model through the supported path; preserve the identity and state.
7. Evaluate the new model against preference/task tests rather than assuming identical behavior.
8. Correct or forget a memory; verify scoped retrieval and restore behavior.
9. Deny a forbidden action despite a profile requesting it.
10. Reject a foreign profile, wrong root/lineage, stale update, and malformed schema.
11. Inject a crash during profile update; recover an intact old or new revision, not mixed state.
12. Verify untrusted content cannot persistently change persona, goals, permissions, or context scope.

Record whether a run is fixture-based, real-model hosted, QEMU, or physical. Existing synthetic model-digest tests do not establish real behavioral continuity under model replacement. Preserve failed evidence; a skipped check is not PASS.

Add a bounded long-session test for preference drift/context isolation and multi-session stale-update cases. No extra agents or parallel execution are required unless existing repository instructions call for them.

## 7. Implementation stages and completion gates

- [ ] Audit current ALLEN code, accepted decisions, active PRs, product interfaces, and identity engagement; produce a dependency map and reconcile stale status text.
- [ ] Define/reuse persona/profile, context, and identity-presentation contracts; document storage ownership and migrations.
- [ ] Implement authoritative profile persistence, subject binding, revisions, and crash-safe edits.
- [ ] Deliver working onboarding/attach and personalization controls in the actual supported product interface.
- [ ] Wire typed context assembly into production inference/tool execution.
- [ ] Implement a minimal general standing-goal kind through existing intent machinery.
- [ ] Deliver scoped memory inspection/correction/forget/export with explicit retention limitations.
- [ ] Integrate shared presentation across available interfaces.
- [ ] Extend continuity, model-change, authorization, isolation, and failure tests.
- [ ] Publish reproducible instructions, compatibility/status matrix, evidence and reviewable PRs.

First release is complete only when customization survives restart and is consumed by real interactions under the same identity, permission boundaries remain enforced, and memory/context controls work as documented. Native provisioning/hardware gaps remain explicit blockers to those particular claims, not reasons to mislabel hosted results.

## Working discipline and final handoff

Implement through isolated branches/worktrees and small dependency-ordered PRs. Respect active owners, candidate freezes, mandatory review, GPU reservations, and existing approval boundaries. Do not rewrite working infrastructure for stylistic reasons. Resolve routine engineering choices autonomously and continue through unblocked work.

Do not present this issue as acceptance of new native formats, additional subjects, unrestricted autonomy, or new permission grants. Record necessary architectural amendments in the established authority before implementing conflicting behavior.

Deliver code, contracts, tested UI/runtime integration, versioned schemas, migration/recovery behavior, tests, and evidence-linked PRs. Finish with:
- what a user can now personalize and how;
- how identity survives rename/restart/model replacement;
- what is actually enforced versus advisory;
- supported memory/context controls and retention limitations;
- exact tests and environments;
- remaining blockers and the next three actions.

The goal is a personal ALLEN users recognize and control, sustained by the existing AIEN architecture—not another chatbot wrapper or competing agent runtime.

title: Allen program: give Allen what Hermes has, in our stack. Start-here prompt for the implementing agent
body:
Drake, 2026-10-18: *"I basically want to make Allen into what I want Allen to be, able to have what Hermes is doing."*

This issue is the start-here prompt for the agent that implements it. It is written to work in any harness (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes). To start the work, tell the agent: **"work on aien-architecture issue <this number>"**, or paste the block below as its first message.

```text
You are the implementing agent for the Allen program: Allen, AIEN's persistent agent, gains the
capabilities of the open-source Hermes Agent, built in our own stack. Drake (the operator, an
engineer who is not a programmer) owns the decisions; you do the work and report in plain English.

GOAL
Allen should be able to do what Hermes does: hold a long conversation without losing the operator's
words, use tools safely in parallel, remember across restarts, write and age its own skills under
rules, reach the operator on messaging platforms, run scheduled jobs that fire at most once, refuse
dangerous actions by a rule it cannot skip, and roll back its own file edits without touching the
operator's. Hermes is the reference for the mechanics, never the code: nothing is copied, everything
is re-implemented in Rust with Omega as the destination (aien-architecture ADR 0024). No Python.

READ FIRST, IN THIS ORDER (do not write code before this list is done)
1. aien-architecture docs/research/hermes-agent-prior-art.md (the study: what Hermes does, what we
   have, the six mechanics judged worth rewriting, licence rule, transfer mapping).
2. aien-architecture#267 (parent) and its six children:
   aien-sovereign-core#664 compaction + token accounting, #665 persist-before-act loop,
   #666 tool batch planning, #667 approval floors + agent-write ledger,
   omega#563 agent-written skills + skill ledger, aegis-runtime#68 delivery + cron guarantees.
   Each child carries its own mechanics list and acceptance test.
3. Allen today: aienos docs/adr/0018-allen-subject-state-object.md (durable subject state),
   aien-architecture docs/adr/0035-persistent-cognitive-entity-boundary-allen.md,
   aienos crates/allen-reflex (decision core), aienos native/kernel/svc/allen_*.c (kernel services),
   aienos docs/ALLEN_PRESENCE_RESEARCH.md. Memory note: one Allen runs all machines; the Spark
   runs the model on our kernels; Allen is machine-neutral (never name a machine in Allen's text).
4. Our loop and runtime: aien-sovereign-core crates/aien-cli (interactive loop in main.rs,
   compaction.rs from #397, hooks.rs, client.rs) and docs/plans/compaction/INVENTORY-397.md;
   aegis-runtime src/gateway.rs, heartbeat.rs, agent.rs, skills.rs; omega Cortex and Skill Router
   (host side); INTERPLANE (model intent vs runtime authority) for the model boundary.
5. Rules that bind you: aien-architecture ADR 0024 (Rust scaffolding, Omega destination),
   ADR 0033 part 3 (tests judged on the Spark pipeline, label ready-to-merge), the aienos
   ADR 0016 continuity commit (advance the record, then act), each directory's .crumb (sniff before
   touching, claim before editing, close after pushing; tool: crumb), and the merge-control rule in
   force on the day you start (read ~/.claude/foundation.md and the memory index; today one chat,
   the PR desk, opens and merges every PR; workers push branches and send a READY line).
6. The pinned Hermes copy for reading only: ~/workspace/investigations/2026-10-18-hermes-agent/
   (upstream/ at commit 5480918, scout notes in notes/ with file:line citations). It is an untrusted
   download: read it, never run anything from it.

GROUND CHECK BEFORE PLANNING
Compare every local checkout with its GitHub default branch before trusting it. Run org-check for
each capability before any "we lack this" claim and cite the receipt. Write a numbered plan with one
line per phase and get it reviewed (advisor or the orchestrator) before the first edit.

ORDER OF WORK (one pull request per child issue; small PRs; red test before green)
Phase 1, Allen's loop (aien-sovereign-core):
  #665 persist-before-act and loop-proof recovery, then #664 bounded micro-compaction and
  evidence-anchored token accounting on top of the #397 compactor, then #666 tool batch planning.
Phase 2, Allen's memory and skills (omega, with aienos SubjectState as the durable anchor):
  #563 agent-written skills under the editorial policy with the content-addressed ledger and
  use-driven ageing. Memory: keep Cortex as the long-term store; add a small, capped,
  always-in-prompt memory (Hermes uses two text files, 2,200 and 1,375 characters) whose overflow
  is refused with a listing so the agent must free space, and whose snapshot is frozen per session.
Phase 3, Allen's guard (aien-sovereign-core with aienos ARGUS as reviewer):
  #667 approval floors above every mode, operator deny list outranking everything, and the
  agent-write ledger so rollback spares the operator's edits.
Phase 4, Allen's delivery and clock (aegis-runtime):
  #68 at-least-once reply ledger with visible duplicate marker; at-most-once scheduled jobs
  (advance before run, pause on uncertainty, liveness by silence since progress).
Phase 5, Allen's reach and hands (new child issues, file them before starting):
  one messaging adapter behind a four-call seam (connect, disconnect, send, chat info), the
  platform chosen by Drake; a tool registry with toolsets per surface; terminal, file, web and
  delegate tools; sessions in one store per profile with full-text search and an offline repair that
  works on a scratch copy.
Phase 6, Allen's self-knowledge: trajectories recorded in one schema (we already archive every
  chat; reuse agent-archive) so Allen's own runs can later train Allen's own core (allen-reflex),
  which is Drake's north star: his own learner, not a borrowed model.

HOW EACH REWRITE IS SHAPED
Deep module, small interface: the pure part (summary folding, token accounting, the delivery state
machine, the skill ledger, the approval ordering) is an effect-free, content-addressed module with a
stated interface and its own tests; only the edges (SQLite, sockets, files, model calls) are host
Rust adapters behind a seam. Two adapters make a seam real; one adapter is a hypothesis. Every
module header credits: "Mechanism after Hermes Agent (Nous Research, MIT, commit 5480918),
re-implemented; no code copied." Verbatim text (for example a prompt rule) puts the MIT notice in
that repository's NOTICE file.

EVIDENCE AND REPORTING
Every claim of done carries the exact test command, its result on the Spark pipeline, and what is
NOT tested. No time, size or speed estimates without a measurement. Speak to Drake in plain English:
what changed, why it matters to Allen, what it means in practice. Update the nearest README and the
Allen front page with every change. When a phase closes, write ~/handoffs/<date>-allen-program.md
(goal, plan, done, next) and record one Cortex lesson per hard bug.

STOP CONDITIONS
Stop and ask Drake only for intent (which messaging platform, which approval floors are his), never
for technical choices. If GitHub refuses with the guard's wait signal, wait; never hammer.
```

body:
## Current release delivery control (2026-10-14)

This issue is the release coordinator under Drake's current direction. Every active workstream delivers candidate-bound evidence here; most implementation capacity goes to trusted native execution, physical GB10, inference correctness and recovery. Synapse, Atlas evaluation and RSI remain bounded parallel deliveries.

**Current delivery ledger:** [2026-10-14 owner directive, workstreams and required evidence](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/190#issuecomment-6178309786). **Reviewable plan update:** [#223](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/pull/223). **Bounded evaluation/RSI tracking:** [architecture #222](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/222), [spark-rsi #54](https://github.com/aien-spark/spark-rsi/issues/54).

RC-1 remains the authorized native freeze in CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md. Its successor is NOT_FROZEN until required merges, consumed dependencies, artifact/model/policy/authority identities, acceptance contracts and clean double-build/recovery evidence are reconciled. Component readiness and hosted reference results cannot become whole-system native PASS by aggregation. The native release requires E1-E6 and physical N1-N7 on the same frozen candidate with controls and independent verdicts.

The earlier component/status table below is a historical program-scope snapshot, not today's implementation inventory. PLAN_AUTHORITY.md and CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md retain authority; milestone status remains in doctrine/ROADMAP.md. Frozen acceptance files and candidate records remain immutable.

---

Tracking issue for the release-readiness program. Drake's decision of 2026-10-10 (session-observer handoff, recorded in memory): AT-1 is REVIEWED and closed administratively, no automatic AT-2, and the principal effort is now **finishing AIEN as one usable system**. This issue runs issue-first like omega#358 and omega#371: milestones are posted here as comments; documents land as PRs to this repository; code and receipts land in their component repositories.

**NOT A MASTER PLAN.** `PLAN_AUTHORITY.md` stands: `doctrine/ARCHITECTURE.md` owns architecture, `doctrine/ROADMAP.md` owns milestone ids, `CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md` owns sequencing. This program produces a gap assessment and a prioritized integration plan, and proposes changes to the execution plan by PR. It claims nothing as implemented from plan wording: code on the live default branches and merged receipts beat every document, and every discrepancy is recorded, not smoothed over.

## 1. The central acceptance test (written first, before any assessment)

One AIEN installation on one machine must do all six of the following in one run, with a receipt for each step, and fail the matching negative control for each step. Working name: **WHOLE-SYSTEM-E2E**.

| step | what must happen | pass condition | negative control |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 install | a clean user account installs AIEN offline from the signed release artifact and starts it | signature verified, services up, install receipt written; no network, no Python, no systemd | a tampered artifact is refused with a named reason |
| E2 objective | an operator submits a real objective through an operator interface (CLI or OSH), for example "turn these three local files into a report and store it" | the objective is recorded with an identity before any work starts | an objective that needs a forbidden effect is refused before execution |
| E3 execute | the runtime plans, routes capabilities, runs the local model for inference, and performs effects through the approval desk | the report exists, every step has a receipt chained to the objective identity | a step that skips the approval desk is caught and the run stops |
| E4 memory | the run writes to Cortex; after a full process restart a second objective that depends on that memory succeeds | the recall is observable in the second run's receipts, from durable storage not process memory | with Cortex storage removed, the second objective fails loud, not silently wrong |
| E5 verify | an independent verifier (judge or evaluator, separate code from the executor) checks the outputs | verifier receipt with verdict identity; same verdict on a second machine | a deliberately corrupted output is rejected by the verifier |
| E6 recover | the runtime is killed mid-objective (SIGKILL) and restarted | the objective finishes from durable state, no effect is performed twice, the receipt chain is unbroken | restart without the durable state gives a named refusal, not a duplicated effect |

Rules for the test: real model weights, no network during the run, Spark first and a second machine for E5, evidence folder immutable once written, verdict identities comparable across machines (as AT-1 did). ## Mission / scope
Deliver **one physical end-to-end user experience**: Raspberry Pi 5 boots **AIENOS without Linux**, ALLEN is the persistent user-facing subject, accepts typed natural-language conversation, makes a measured local decision, dispatches heavier inference/program work over an authenticated link to DGX Spark, and presents streamed progress plus independently verifiable output. The Spark may remain Linux-hosted for this finite integration demonstration; **native AIENOS-on-Spark is a separate N1–N7 release track**.

This is a **finite cross-repository integration tracker, not a new master architecture**. Parent release ledger: #190; persona/continuity: #159; first encounter: aien-spark/aienos#396. Preserve PLAN_AUTHORITY.md, CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md, frozen native release candidates, Crumbs, active branches, and historical receipts. New code and research choices are replaceable by evidence; never silently redefine existing claims, Turing units, or authorization boundaries.

## Source-based inventory (inspected October 16, 2026)
- Pi physical Ethernet: aienos `native/kernel/dev/pi5_gem.c`, `docs/native/PI5-NET-3-RUNS.md`: link, loopback, TX, DMA confinement, **no demonstrated external RX→Spark round trip**. Existing umbrella aienos#33.
- M6-B secure transport: aienos `native/net/aienos_sec.c`: hosted protocol code; physical Pi binding **not proved**.
- Native user path: aienos `native/kernel/core/lifecycle.c`, `line_rx.c`, `fbcon.c`, `agent_cmd.c`: native lifecycle and terminal pieces, Pi command-script qualifications, not the finished conversation UI. Reuse aienos#396.
- Local routing: aienos `crates/allen-reflex/src/action.rs`, `tower.rs`: 15 command/exam decisions; Tower **library only, not wired to Pi**. Held-out exact REFLEX 21/26; nearest 23/26; perceptron 22/26 (Spark host benchmarks, NOT Pi).
- Spark generation: aien-sovereign-core `crates/aien-inference-abi/src/generation.rs`: controller still says **no production caller**; 30B ForwardPass adapter is **OPEN PR #557**. Omegese mask crate `crates/aien-omegese-constraint` merged via #555, host-only checks.
- Executable path: omega `tools/omegese/omegese.c` → omega_emit → canonical OSC IR → checker2; execution/receipt must be bound to objective and hardware, not inferred from syntax acceptance.
- Background work: aegis-runtime `src/orchestration/workflow.rs`: DAG state explicitly memory-only. Hosted durable objective/effect reconciliation exists in sovereign-core `crates/aien-runtime/src/objective.rs`; current recovery tracking sc#379.
- INTERPLANE `rust/crates/interplane-core/src/lib.rs`: tool-call translation and canonical wire semantics, **not scheduler, network link or authority**. Native adapter conformance is separately tracked at interplane#101.
- Existing optimization/research: omega#445 representation experiment, omega#475–#480 generalization, sovereign-core#494 KV residency. Do not duplicate these.

## Frozen acceptance to author as first PR (not a release claim)
Declare `ALLEN-PI-SPARK-E2E-v1`, recording exact commit/image/model/IR/transport/protocol identities, independent verifier and negative controls, using a user-selected request AFTER cold boot:
1. Pi boots AIENOS, presents the existing #396 greeting and accepts a live user turn, with owner/guest and lock behavior intact.
2. Pi local decision produces a typed decision with an explicit unknown/clarify route, logged latency and correct authority separation.
3. Physical Pi Ethernet ↔ Spark authenticated session carries a bounded, versioned, correlated request and stream; reject wrong peer, replay, stale id, disconnection.
4. Spark performs **real GB10 model inference**, streams text to Pi; structured program request produces **real model-generated Omegese**.
5. Omegese → omega_emit → checker2; independently verified result and objective-bound execution receipt (not just accepted syntax). Bad code, unauthorized effect, corrupt result all refuse.
6. More than one dependent/parallel task, truthful progress, approval, cancel and crash/reconnect recovery; no repeated committed effect.
7. Record TTFT, completion p50/p95, memory, tokens, byte cost, throughput and measured energy where instrumentation exists. No invented numbers or conflating Turing-yield V0 with token throughput.
8. Verify local-only behavior and honest Spark-offline degradation, owner subject/memory intact after cold reboot.

**First product-level PASS requires one same-candidate physical run**, receipts from each step, negative controls and independent evaluation. QEMU/host passes are prerequisites, not substitutions.

## Swarm operating protocol
- Workstreams must use **non-overlapping file ownership**, separate branches/worktrees and small PRs. Inspect HEAD + open PRs + worktree claims before editing. Coordinate conflicts through this ticket, not concurrent edits to the same file.
- Lane A: hardware Pi networking + authenticated transport; Lane B: Pi native conversation (existing aienos#396) and local REFLEX routing; Lane C: Spark bidirectional inference worker; Lane D: Omegese GPU generation integration (depends on sc#557); Lane E: Omega checked execution/evidence; Lane F: delegated DAG/resume; Lane G: acceptance/evaluation.

- Do not create a second subject identity, Store, agent daemon, permission framework, network fabric, general-purpose language, or dashboard. Reuse or retire implementations based on proof, not loyalty.

- No autonomous merge/deploy/production-enable implied by this tracking issue. Respect project review/release controls.

## Critical path
Physical Pi RX/TX + authenticated link → streaming hosted Spark inference → Omegese model→checked executable→verified result → durable task orchestration → full Pi/Spark acceptance. Native greeting/UI and Pi classifier calibration can develop in parallel. Native Spark OS release is downstream and remains separately gated by #190.

## Non-goals
Do not gate the first usable Allen on native Spark GB10 drivers, voice, browser/mobile frontends, novel Turing theory, model training or speculative kernel research. Those are subsequent qualified streams.

Leaf issues will be linked in the next comment after creation; do not mark stages complete from plans or merged library code alone.

title: ALLEN first encounter: native AIENOS boot, “Hello, Humanity.”, introduction and remembered user name
body:
## Product objective

Deliver ALLEN's first encounter as the native AIENOS startup experience.

**Drake's requested experience:**

> Power on. AIENOS flashes briefly while the system boots quickly. ALLEN's visual entity appears and greets the user with **“Hello, Humanity.”** The user can then introduce themselves, tell ALLEN their name and preferred form of address, and continue interacting. With permission, ALLEN remembers them and greets them personally after a later boot.

The primary deliverable is this coherent user experience on the physical Pi 5 running AIENOS, followed by the same presentation/behavior contracts on the Spark. Existing boot, identity, persistence, input and inference work supports the encounter.

### Authority and related work

- Parent product workstream: [aien-architecture #159 — ALLEN persona, onboarding, personalization and continuity](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/159).
- Release coordination: [aien-architecture #190](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/190).
- Follow `PLAN_AUTHORITY.md`, `CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md`, applicable repository instructions and current candidate ownership.
- This is a finite product/integration issue, **not a new master plan, agent framework, identity system or authorization grant**.
- Do not reorder native Spark qualification or claim that Pi results qualify Spark.
- No physical reboot, device write, firmware change, key operation or deployment is authorized by this issue; use the existing separately approved attended procedure.

## Reuse: work already done or in progress

Checked against GitHub on 2026-10-16. Refresh source heads, PR states and local worktree ownership before implementation.

| Existing work | Observed status | Use here |
|---|---|---|
| [AIENOS #256](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/pull/256), GOP framebuffer console | Merged | Reuse framebuffer discovery/handoff and bounded drawing; add encounter presentation. |
| [AIENOS #24](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/issues/24), keyboard after firmware exit | Closed as completed, QEMU acceptance | Reuse input implementation; qualify the actual Pi display/keyboard path. |
| [AIENOS #260](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/pull/260), native ALLEN genesis/restore | Merged | Preserve existing subject identity and restore rules. |
| [Core #302](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-sovereign-core/pull/302), persona profile | Merged, hosted | Reuse relevant profile contracts and revision semantics. Its display name names ALLEN, not the human. |
| [Core #303](https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-sovereign-core/pull/303), scoped memory | Merged, hosted | Preserve ownership, consent/scoping and honest correction/forget limits; integrate through canonical native Store/Cortex rather than another database. |
| [AIENOS #370](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/pull/370), Pi lifecycle | Merged, physical qualification runs | Reuse generation, approval, preference, saved object and recall behavior. The current card script is qualification input, not the live encounter. |
| [AIENOS #379](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/pull/379), REFLEX, and [#381](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/pull/381), Tower | Merged | Reuse typed decision work where useful; do not recreate it or treat it as a graphical avatar. |
| [Omega #69](https://github.com/aien-spark/omega/pull/69), Visor | Merged, terminal-first semantic viewport | Reuse appropriate boundaries; this is not the visual ALLEN entity. |
| [AIENOS #392](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/pull/392), dual-invalid recovery image | Open at inspection | Coordinate with its owner; do not start competing recovery work. |
| [AIENOS #85](https://github.com/aien-spark/aienos/issues/85), native voice | Open | Preserve its direction that voice is the eventual default and text the fallback. Text can deliver the first encounter increment without pretending speech already exists. |

No matching issue/PR for the exact visual greeting-to-introduction experience was found in the preceding check. Unpushed local work was not inspected; reconcile it before creating new implementation branches.

## 1. Experience specification

### Startup and arrival

1. Power on into the declared AIENOS installation.
2. Briefly show **AIENOS**, then transition into ALLEN's visual presence.
3. Keep routine diagnostic output out of the normal encounter. Retain a deliberate troubleshooting path and truthful failure/recovery display.
4. Display exactly **“Hello, Humanity.”** with this capitalization and punctuation.
5. Make the input usable as ALLEN invites the user to introduce themselves.

ALLEN's exact visual form and movement have **not** been selected. First produce a small storyboard/visual proposal and obtain Drake's design choice before production visual assets. Do not silently substitute a generic dashboard or claim an existing text console is the finished entity.

Suggested follow-up copy, reviewable rather than frozen:

> “I'm ALLEN. What would you like me to call you?”

The opening greeting should be deterministic and available without waiting for a large language model to invent it. Input and subsequent responses must accurately reflect readiness; do not use an animation to conceal unavailable conversation.

### Introduction and permission

- Accept a fresh live introduction after boot, including “I'm Drake.”
- Extract a **proposed** preferred human name; show it and ask whether to remember it.
- Explicit confirmation binds the exact proposed value to the current session/profile revision.
- A denial saves nothing; a correction replaces the proposal before confirmation.
- Skip/guest mode is available and does not create a named owner profile.
- Other personal details are retained only with explicit permission, not automatically inferred from conversation.
- A person's preferred name is separate from ALLEN's identity, ALLEN's chosen display name, authentication, machine ownership and capability grants.
- Name changes, inspection and forgetting remain available later through the supported operator path.

### Return after reboot

After the authorized owner state is available, restore the consented preferred name and greet the user personally. The name must come from durable state, not a staging file, repeated prompt or process memory.

Locked/corrupt/unavailable state must never be interpreted as an empty new installation. Do not reveal stored personal details before owner access is established or silently reprovision ALLEN.

## 2. Implementation boundaries

Start by inspecting the current code and evidence:

- `native/boot/efi_gop.c`
- `native/kernel/core/fbcon.[ch]`, `console.c`
- `native/kernel/dev/usb_kbd.c`, `usb_hid.c` and platform bindings
- `native/kernel/core/lifecycle.c`, `lifecycle_fsm.[ch]`, `agent_cmd.[ch]`
- `native/kernel/svc/cortex_store.c`, `cortex_journal.c`, Store and continuity services
- `crates/allen-reflex/`, existing native inference bridge
- hosted `aien-allen-profile` / `aien-allen-memory` contracts and architecture #159
- `docs/native/PI5-7-LIFECYCLE-RUNS.md`

The current framebuffer console supports ASCII text; it is not evidence of a full multilingual encounter renderer. Establish supported text/input coverage and preserve the user's spelling; do not silently truncate or corrupt names.

Use one native encounter state machine to coordinate arrival, greeting, introduction, name confirmation, committing, conversation, guest, locked and recovery states. The presentation layer consumes typed runtime events and cannot directly bypass capability or Store policy.

Reuse the existing native persistence owner. Any missing native human-name record/schema needs an explicit reviewed contract, subject binding, revision/consent semantics and migration. Do not blindly copy the hosted filesystem store or reinterpret ALLEN's `display_name` as the user's name.

The product input must be live after firmware exit. `AGENT.CMD` remains qualification-only. SSH, a web page or Linux keyboard handling is not evidence of the native local experience.

Keep keyboard operation and reduced motion available. UI rendering/animation must have bounded memory and redraw costs and yield to input. Separate UI readiness from inference readiness.

## 3. Work packages

- [ ] **Audit and ownership:** reconcile existing work, open PRs, local branches/worktrees and actual Pi display/input/boot configuration; document reuse and the remaining gap.
- [ ] **Storyboard and visual choice:** boot mark, entity arrival, greeting, introduction, confirmation and returning greeting; select ALLEN's appearance with Drake.
- [ ] **Physical display/input proof:** demonstrate framebuffer output and usable post-firmware input on the actual Pi under an authorized window.
- [ ] **Native encounter renderer/state machine:** implement the selected presentation, exact opening greeting, keyboard input/focus, reduced motion, readiness and error branches.
- [ ] **Consented human-name persistence:** bind to existing subject/Store, crash-safe consent/profile activation, correction/forget and neutral locked/recovery handling.
- [ ] **Live conversation integration:** connect the encounter to existing ALLEN/lifecycle paths; show only real listening/thinking/responding states; preserve cancellation and approval boundaries.
- [ ] **Boot responsiveness:** measure and optimize startup without weakening initialization, hiding failures or artificially holding the logo. Record power-on -> first pixel, AIENOS entry -> greeting/input ready, and request -> first response separately. Freeze timing targets after measuring firmware/platform costs; no numerical speed claim exists yet.
- [ ] **Physical first-encounter qualification:** execute the acceptance cases below at one pinned candidate, with independent verdict and retained evidence.
- [ ] **Spark adaptation:** reuse the encounter contracts; qualify Spark-specific display/input/inference independently when its native prerequisites close.

Use small reviewable PRs and regression/negative controls. Do not rewrite working reference implementations for language preference or expand into an unrelated voice, networking or agent-framework project.

## 4. Acceptance: one complete encounter

On the physical Pi, using a frozen candidate and a real display/input path:

1. Cold power-on -> brief AIENOS mark -> ALLEN appears -> exact **“Hello, Humanity.”**
2. User introduces themselves with a value chosen **after boot**, through live input.
3. ALLEN proposes the correct human preferred name and requests permission to remember it.
4. Deny once: no persistent name. Correct and explicitly confirm: only the confirmed name is committed.
5. ALLEN acknowledges successful persistence and accepts a subsequent conversational request.
6. Restart without introduction/name staging files or retyped name; after owner access, greet the same user personally.
7. Change and forget the preferred name; restart and verify the intended behavior.
8. Test skip/guest, ambiguous consent, long/Unicode/control-character input, wrong unlock, unavailable model, missing/corrupt Store and disconnected input.
9. On backed-up qualification media, interrupt profile activation at registered boundaries: recover previous or new valid state, never a partly saved introduction.
10. Untrusted text/model output/stored instructions cannot consent, change identity, grant permissions or overwrite the confirmed name.
11. Retain exact source/image/firmware/model identities, timing measurements, output/state hashes, controls and an independent verdict.

A clean shutdown then power removal is valuable recall evidence but not an interrupted-write test. Hosted/QEMU runs remain their own evidence class. Screenshots or scripted demos alone do not establish physical end-to-end acceptance.

## Done when

A person can power on AIENOS, meet ALLEN, see **“Hello, Humanity.”**, introduce themselves naturally, choose what is remembered, continue interacting, and return after reboot to the same persistent ALLEN recognizing their confirmed preferred name.

Report exact implemented behavior, reused components, candidate and physical evidence, timing limits, text/voice support, and remaining platform/sovereignty dependencies. Do not mark this done from individual component passes alone.

title: [ALLEN Pi/Spark A] Physical Pi 5 Ethernet RX/TX and authenticated Spark session
body:
Parent: https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/231. Existing networking umbrella: #33. This ticket is **the first end-to-end hardware blocker**, not a replacement network stack.

## Inspected code / gap
- `native/kernel/dev/pi5_gem.[ch]` implements bounded RP1 GEM descriptors and transmit/loopback; `docs/native/PI5-NET-3-RUNS.md` physically proves link, PHY/local loopback and wire TX. External ingress RX and peer-confirmed receive are **NOT PROVEN**.
- `native/kernel/dev/pi5_net.c`, `pi5_pcie.c`, `net_udp.c` provide Pi bring-up and reusable freestanding Ethernet/ARP/IPv4/UDP logic.
- `native/net/aienos_sec.[ch]` already implements M6-B crypto-secure control transport (host-tested, I/O-free); do not reinvent crypto or confuse tested transport logic with physical link proof.
- `native/kernel/core/lifecycle.c` owns native unlocked/locked policy. Pi RP1 DMA is weaker than Spark SMMU; preserve the explicitly bounded bounce window, descriptor validation, bus-master quiescence.

## Deliver in small independent PRs
1. Physical bidirectional GEM Ethernet frame path: Pi can RX a fresh externally transmitted, payload-checked frame and TX an acknowledged one. Negative controls for bad RX length, invalid descriptors, checksums and DMA bounds; leave driver quiet on failure.
2. Minimal static-IP peer path for Pi ↔ Spark (ARP + IPv4 + UDP or another justified, minimal framed transport) using existing net code. Dynamic address / Internet networking are optional and NOT on this critical path.
3. Bind `aienos_sec` to Pi physical transport and implement/test the matching Spark endpoint using existing documented handshake/session primitives. Owner-approved real identity enrollment only; no TEST key in production.
4. Add bounded session framing, correlation and loss/retry/backpressure/cancel, with wrong-key, replay, stale sequence, truncated message and disconnect negative cases. Agree wire message shape with the **protocol lane** before freezing it.
5. Record transport throughput/RTT, CPU time, memory, drops, reconnect behavior, hashes, firmware/driver/image pins.

## Proof / done
Host-fake tests and QEMU first, then attended real Pi + Spark. Real physical duplex request/response using **fresh random nonce generated after boot**, identical payload byte hash verified on each endpoint, plus negative controls; signed/replay-safe handshake and recovery after cable pull. Show the actual peer-receive logs, not only a Pi TX-completion bit. An unauthorized test, flashing, physical reboot, secret change, GPU stop or deploy is not authorized by this issue; follow existing owner procedures. Do not claim native AIENOS Spark qualification.
