title: [ALLEN Pi/Spark C] Versioned bounded task/event/receipt protocol between native Pi and Spark
body:
Parent: https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/231. Protocol owner: aien-protocols; consumers aienos physical-link lane and aien-sovereign-core Spark worker lane. This is the **control-plane application schema**, not another network stack, INTERPLANE replacement, agent scheduler or authorization layer.

## Existing source / compatibility
- AIENOS `native/net/aienos_sec.[ch]` secures a byte channel; `native/kernel/dev/net_udp.c` constructs low-level frames.
- INTERPLANE `rust/crates/interplane-core/src/{lib,types,validate}.rs` canonicalizes model tool requests, decisions and results; core explicitly **authorizes and executes nothing**. Native conformance of that adapter is already interplane#101; do not duplicate it.
- Hosted durable objectives: aien-sovereign-core `crates/aien-runtime/src/objective.rs` uses identity-bound objective records. Native ALLEN identity stays authority at AIENOS.
- AEGIS `src/orchestration/workflow.rs` has task states, but not a durable cross-node API.

## Deliver
1. Inventory existing specs first; choose a small **versioned** binary or canonical-bytes envelope, with bounded fields, strict max frame and message size, fragment/reassembly rules and unknown-version refusal. Do not create a new format if an existing schema meets the same constraints.
2. Declare authenticated peer/session id, user-subject reference (no key material), objective id, parent/child task ids, idempotence key, ordinal, request/response/event type, payload digest, effect class, protocol version and limit. Keep trusted/untrusted provenance distinct.
3. Events: accepted, queued, running, streamed text chunk, waiting_for_approval, completed, failed, cancelled, uncertain_after_disconnect, resume_snapshot, receipt reference; status must be derived from authoritative execution state.
4. Spell out exactly-once limitations: deduplicate retries and reconcile uncertain effects against existing authoritative ledger. Transport ACK is not execution completion. Local model route has no implied authorization.
5. Add a C freestanding decoder/encoder test fixture and Rust counterpart/golden vectors; fuzz malformed/truncated/out-of-order frames, duplicated ids, forged completion/approval and subject mismatch; version downgrade refuses.
6. Provide adapter mapping into INTERPLANE **only for actual tool calls**; no authority migration or separate INTERPLANE transport promise.

## Acceptance
Cross-language byte-exact fixtures, full replay tests, fuzz/mutation controls, offline binary examples and diagram of trust boundaries. Physical round trip is qualified by aienos networking lane; Spark worker consumes this stable contract. Protocol types do not grant capabilities or permissions.

title: [ALLEN Pi/Spark E] Omegese-constrained generation through real OWN-30B ForwardPass
body:
Parent: https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/231. Dependency: **open PR #557** (ADR 0004 step 3 ForwardPass adapter), then the reviewed controller step that actually becomes production. Do not race PR #557's files or quietly switch live inference defaults.

## Code-backed gap
- `crates/aien-inference-abi/src/generation.rs` explicitly says GenerationController is pure addition and **no production caller** uses it yet.
- Merged #550 created generation controller + Constraint; merged #555 added opt-in `crates/aien-omegese-constraint` with `SubprocessOracle` → Omega `omegese next --machine`. The #555 evidence is **host-only**, not GB10 model-generated programs.
- Omega `tools/omegese/omegese.c`, `docs/one_layer/OMEGESE.md`: Omegese emits omega_emit op lists and OSC canonical IR, checked by checker2. It is a program-generation representation, **not** the chat or network wire format.

## Work packages
1. After #557 merges or is explicitly consumed at a pinned tested head, integrate the real 30B `ForwardPass` with controller and audited generate path, preserving off/default byte-identical behavior and KV identity/rollback invariants.
2. Make the real model accept an opt-in `ProgramGeneration` request with signature, effect scope, max tokens, deadline and Omegese constraint. Keep ordinary chat unconstrained unless explicitly requested.
3. Evaluate 60 pre-registered held-out program tasks (or reuse existing frozen omega#445/OMEGESE trial protocol where compatible); compare uncontrolled vs grammar only vs prefix guard; report checker acceptance separately from **functional correctness**.
4. Reduce oracle/mask costs only after measuring them (subprocess implementation currently scans vocab, and its host receipt reported double-digit ms per masked token); sparse output head is a **separate profiled optimization**, not required for the first real generated program.
5. Pass actual text through exact Omegese emitter + omega_emit + checker2, then hand a candidate to the authorized Omega execution/evidence lane; no automatic effect based only on grammar correctness.
6. Measure GPU/CPU/transfer/token/mask overhead, TTFT, total duration, output fidelity, model digest and replay receipts; never infer pass from host-only EchoChain tests.

## Acceptance
With a real pinned model/GB10 run, one user-selected function task is emitted as Omegese, checker2 accepts, an independent functional verifier checks execution outcome, invalid source is rejected and an effect without grant cannot execute. Negative controls: truncation, malformed model text, stale KV, wrong function signature, forced illegal token, corrupted compiled bytes. Do not claim general-purpose autonomous Omegese orchestration.

title: [ALLEN Pi/Spark F] Objective-bound Omegese → OSC → executable result with independent receipt
body:
Parent: https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/231. Pairs with aien-sovereign-core Omegese real-model-generation lane; **this issue owns the checked execution/evidence path**, not model sampling, user chat, or a new compiler.

## Inspected baseline
- `tools/omegese/omegese.c`: Omegese `emit` maps human-free model program to `omega_emit` op list.
- `tools/omega_emit/`, `src/checker2/`, `src/compiler/` and `docs/one_layer/OMEGESE.md`: canonical OSC IR, typed/checker rules and execution machinery already exist. Omegese spec explicitly says trust chain Omegese -> omega_emit -> OSC binary IR -> checker2 -> signed receipt.
- Existing omega#445 representation comparison and omega#475–#480 compositional-generalization experiments are already tracked. Do not repeat or score on their sealed held-outs; reuse only declared comparable fixtures.
- Existing checker limitations matter: omega#465 reports certain one-path ownership/borrow cases were admitted. Never equate front-end grammar acceptance with full proof of safety.

## Bounded deliverables
1. Build one thin callable `verified-program` entrypoint over existing emitter/checker/loader: input program bytes, declared function signature, bounded inputs, objective id, compiler/policy/build digests and execution tier; output exact checked IR hash, runtime output hash, rejection code, resource measurements and receipt refs.
2. Preflight checker2 and independent code image validation immediately before execution; refuse changed bytes, unsupported calls/opcodes/side effects, traps and unknown versions. Keep effect authorization in AIENOS/runtime authority; Omega checker is not authority.
3. Start with deterministic bounded scalar/Omegese user-selected functions (gcd, integer sequence transform); GPU kernel execution only after showing the specific IR lowering supports the actual hardware operation and has its own device receipt. **Do not call a CPU result 'GPU kernel launched'.**
4. Provide an independent verifier or existing verifier adapter that recomputes expected result and validates provenance, IR and output. Include deliberately incorrect but parseable program, checker rejection, tampered IR/output, stale objective and unauthorized effect negatives.
5. Record compiler/version/model pinned digests, host/QEMU evidence and separately physical GB10 when actually used. Keep reusable artifacts content-addressed and traceable to originating user objective.

## Acceptance
A fresh program produced by the model generation lane passes emitter + checker2 + authorized execution and returns a verified numerical result to Pi. Repeat on fixed reference functions; corrupted output/code produces FAIL. No broad 'all Omegese runs on GPU' claim, no duplicate language or memory store.

title: [ALLEN Pi/Spark G] Recoverable delegated DAG with Pi-owned objective and truthful progress
body:
Parent: https://github.com/aien-spark/aien-architecture/issues/231. Depends on Pi↔Spark typed protocol and Spark worker lanes. Existing aien-sovereign-core#379 owns host-side durable objective/effect recovery; do not reimplement it in AEGIS.

## Code-backed gap
- `src/orchestration/workflow.rs` dependency-aware DAG explicitly says state is **in memory only and does not survive a restart**.
- `src/agent.rs` AgentEngine already handles inference, tool dispatcher, retries, cancellation and event bus. Tools and their receipts must pass through existing runtime authority rather than inference-proposed action alone.
- aien-sovereign-core `crates/aien-runtime/src/objective.rs` records objective ids/validity; core#379 covers effect resume/reconcile.
- `interplane` canonical tool requests and results are model-execution boundary; core itself grants nothing; native counterpart conformance interplane#101 is separately tracked.
- `aienos/crates/allen-reflex/src/tower.rs` routes test gates and caches exact receipt identities only; it is **not** already a durable user-task DAG.

## Work
1. Define how a Pi-owned durable user objective binds to a Spark DAG and each task id. Reuse the existing canonical objective/effect ledger on their respective authorities; avoid duplicating a second source of truth in `aegis-runtime`.
2. Persist or reconstruct DAG state from authoritative durable records. Distinguish accepted/queued/running/waiting approval/completed/failed/cancelled/uncertain after disconnect; events are hints, not commitments.
3. Support concurrent independent tasks, dependency order, per-task quotas, cancel, task reassignment and dedup by request+effect id; report partial results and truthful status over the Pi schema.
4. Gate every real tool call via INTERPLANE mapping and the existing authorization/approval desk. Deny stale/foreign/forged grants; never retry a possibly committed external effect without reconciliation.
5. Fault injection: kill Spark worker between approve and effect, after effect before ACK, cut link mid-stream, Pi reboot, duplicate messages, cancellation races and dependency failure. No duplicate final effect.
6. Produce a non-fake demo: Pi asks for a bounded two-task computation, Spark executes parallel independent steps and a dependent verified result; Allen can chat while tasks continue.

## Acceptance
Real AEGIS DAG within physical Pi/Spark integrated run, after shutdown/restart sees exact state from records, emits no false `completed`, resends no committed effect, and exposes verifiable task/receipt tree. Host fakes plus physical run evidence separated. Never run unapproved machine mutations.

title: Native GB10: replace Linux RM/UVM dependency with an AIENOS backend, through first compute
body:
## Goal

Remove the Linux NVIDIA RM/UVM driver dependency from a **native AIENOS GB10 execution path**, reusing Omega's code generation and compute semantics. The first end-to-end exit is deliberately small: boot AIENOS on the physical Spark, initialize the GB10 through an AIENOS-owned backend, run one known integer vector calculation, verify every output, and quiesce/release resources correctly.

This is the successor to characterization issue #36, not a claim that the driver already exists. Full model inference, broad CUDA compatibility, and replacement of vendor-signed device firmware are outside this first milestone. Preserve the working Linux-hosted backend as a reference during development.

Requested by Drake on 2026-10-08 following the CUDA-dependency review. This issue authorizes a scoped implementation workstream, not an unattended reboot, device reset, firmware change, or a change to the governing execution order.

## Authority and prerequisites

Follow [AIENOS plan authority](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/main/docs/PLAN_AUTHORITY.md), [ROADMAP](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/main/ROADMAP.md), [governing architecture](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), and [whole-system execution plan](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture/blob/main/CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md). **NOT A MASTER PLAN.**

The whole-system plan records an unresolved native-order conflict in aien-dev/aien-architecture#163. Do not resolve it implicitly through this work. Coordinate with the existing PCI/storage/input/rollback lanes; reuse their changes rather than creating parallel implementations. Device-mutating and physical gates remain behind their governing prerequisites and existing authorization procedures. Host-only interface, parser, fixture, and refusal work can proceed where it does not conflict.

Native input/recovery, boot rollback, physical memory authority and the relevant storage/trust dependencies must be demonstrated before the corresponding hardware steps. Existing #31, #32, #34 and #35 retain ownership of storage, trust, CPU inference and continuity. This GPU issue must not delay the CPU-first native milestone or claim to close those issues.

ADR 0019 was accepted in #282 while this inspection was underway. Link #285 as a conditional prerequisite: the first cut that reuses or persists a **domain-1 kernel resource number** must implement its per-resource incarnation counter in the same cut. Do not equate that counter with handle-slot generations or Omega world epochs. Do not assume every GPU-private allocation automatically belongs to domain 1; define the mapping explicitly.

## Inspected code and concrete gaps

Read-only source inspection on 2026-10-08; no builds, tests, hardware access, or qualification runs were performed for this issue.

Inspected snapshots:
- AIENOS code: `fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1`; subsequent docs-only ADR #282 merge: `bf475a089d2824e0c923c42e73f948cc65c87c32`.
- Omega: `2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55`.
- PHYSICS: `6d7cf0d4d8eb2cda7b512100ff6058e25dbb3ddf`, the dependency selected by the inspected Omega `physics.lock`. Newer PHYSICS main must not silently replace the pinned dependency.

| Code read | Finding and implementation consequence |
| --- | --- |
| [nvrm/nvrm.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/physics/blob/6d7cf0d4d8eb2cda7b512100ff6058e25dbb3ddf/nvrm/nvrm.h) and [m16/m16_native.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/physics/blob/6d7cf0d4d8eb2cda7b512100ff6058e25dbb3ddf/m16/m16_native.h) | The current backend explicitly uses Linux NVIDIA device files, RM/UVM objects and ioctls. `M16NativeContext` embeds `Nvrm`; `NvrmMem` assumes identical CPU/GPU virtual addresses. This is a userspace client of the existing driver, not a portable hardware driver. |
| [src/omega_gpu_session.c](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55/src/omega_gpu_session.c) and [src/omega_gpu_session.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55/src/omega_gpu_session.h) | The inference APIs share a persistent session that directly calls `nvrm_open`, `nvrm_alloc_gpu_uncached` and M16 submission functions. It also uses pthread mutexes and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`. Merely replacing an ioctl wrapper will not make this freestanding. Preserve its reservation, completion and failure behavior. |
| [src/omega_gpu_engine.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55/src/omega_gpu_engine.h) and [src/omega_blackwell_engine.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55/src/omega_blackwell_engine.h) | An `OmegaGpuBackend` callback interface and a Blackwell backend already exist for the vector engine. Reuse/extend the existing interface where appropriate; do not invent a second job/result/state machine. It is not proof that the persistent inference session is already abstracted. Some status comments are historical and must be reconciled against implementation/evidence. |
| [src/omega_blackwell_codegen.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55/src/omega_blackwell_codegen.h) and [src/omega_blackwell_qmd.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/omega/blob/2ae8677c604fb1b9566d27412cff7b0339e5df55/src/omega_blackwell_qmd.h) | Existing Blackwell instruction generation, QMD and constant-bank builders are reuse candidates. Hardware assumptions still need validation after replacing the driver-created context. Do not start a second compiler. |
| [crates/aienos-accel/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/crates/aienos-accel/src/lib.rs) | Existing pure identity/BAR decoding and discovery diagnostics are reusable facts/fixtures. They do not establish device ownership or native compute. Keep discovery free of ambient device authority. |
| [native/kernel/dev/pci.c](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/dev/pci.c) and [native/kernel/dev/pci.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/dev/pci.h) | `pci_mcfg_parse` skips every segment except 0. The recorded Spark topology puts GB10 on segment 15. Also, `pci_enumerate` calls `size_bars`, which writes configuration space even without a BAR-allocation window. It is **not a read-only characterization API**. Multi-segment discovery and a genuinely non-mutating probe are concrete prerequisites. |
| [native/kernel/mm/mmu.c](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/mm/mmu.c) and [native/kernel/include/ck.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/include/ck.h) | `ck_mmio_map` / `ck_mmio_try_map` and `ck_dma_alloc` exist. The latter is a bump allocator in a fixed DMA pool, not a reclaiming GPU memory manager. Kernel mapping helpers alone are not the resource-scoped, revocable accelerator service required by the architecture. |
| [native/kernel/core/smmu_svc.c](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/core/smmu_svc.c) and [native/kernel/core/smmu.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/core/smmu.h) | Segment-aware `ck_dma_confine` and two-level stream tables already exist. Reuse them; older roadmap comments claiming only linear tables are stale. The service has one selected SMMU, bounded stream slots and a single confined window per stream; named devices behind another SMMU are refused. Prove the GB10's actual translation route before extending or claiming confinement. |
| [native/kernel/arch/gic.c](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/arch/gic.c) | Existing GIC initialization and `ck_irq_enable` are not evidence of a complete MSI-X/ITS/LPI path; this enable function refuses INTIDs >= 1020. The GPU interrupt route needs its own implementation/inventory and physical evidence. |
| [native/kernel/core/ipc.h](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/native/kernel/core/ipc.h) | Existing capability lookup/rights/derivation/revocation and slot-generation checks are building blocks. They do not yet constitute the full GPU resource contract. |

Read alongside [docs/GB10_NATIVE_ACCELERATOR_BOUNDARY.md](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/docs/GB10_NATIVE_ACCELERATOR_BOUNDARY.md) and [docs/GB10_PLATFORM_TOPOLOGY.md](https://github.com/aien-dev/aienos/blob/fa209e454dda90d933076e5fd1f333731fd9a3c1/docs/GB10_PLATFORM_TOPOLOGY.md). Recorded BDF/BAR addresses and interrupt counts are observations, not constants to hard-code. The topology document's unresolved items must be rechecked against newer code and actual platform evidence.

## Implementation cuts

### A. Dependency map and a freestanding backend boundary

- Inventory current callers of NVRM/M16 across the vector engine, persistent inference session, numerical launchers and resident runtime. Record which are migrated by each cut; no whole-project independence claim from migrating one function.
- Map every driver-provided responsibility: device/firmware initialization, context creation, address spaces, allocation, GPU page tables, channel/queue creation, submit token/doorbell, completion, interrupts, error reporting and teardown.
- Reuse the existing `OmegaGpuBackend` where it fits. Factor genuinely shared hardware encoding from Linux-only allocation/synchronization. Provide explicit platform services for clocks, waiting, locking, allocation and diagnostics.
- Keep Linux RM/UVM state private to its backend. Native contracts use typed resource handles, explicit lengths, rights and CPU/GPU address distinctions. Do not expose a Linux fd or unchecked physical pointer as authority.
- Preserve separate buffer, code and queue lifetimes. Define version/capability negotiation, refusal of unsupported operations, resource limits and concurrency. No silent Linux, CPU or remote fallback in a test claiming native GPU execution.
- Deliver a freestanding link target and backend contract tests before device initialization. No production use of test-only clock/reset hooks.

### B. Native discovery and bounded device ownership

- Extend/reuse PCI discovery across firmware-declared segments and bus ranges; test nonzero starting buses, bridge ranges, malformed/overlapping entries, arithmetic overflow, absent devices and capacity exhaustion.
- Split non-mutating discovery from BAR sizing/assignment and bus-master changes. Instrument fake config access and require **zero configuration writes** for the discovery-only test.
- Validate GPU identity and firmware-described register windows without assuming Linux-observed BDF, addresses, or CPU/bus address equivalence.
- Add capability-bound MMIO, DMA and interrupt resources through the existing authority system. Validate rights/ranges and revoke through real enforcement, not bookkeeping alone.
- Resolve and document the GB10's actual DMA/fabric translation path. Do not assume a PCI configuration endpoint proves every GPU memory transaction traverses the existing SMMU window. Refuse operation when confinement cannot be established.
- Reuse segment-aware IORT/SMMU logic; extend only demonstrated gaps. Audit multi-SMMU selection and fault reporting so GPU faults do not discard another device's evidence.
- Implement the required interrupt route, or document and separately qualify a strictly bounded polling subset if the hardware protocol permits it. Polling does not count as interrupt support.

**Cut B exit:** native device ownership is demonstrated with bounded permissions and revocation. This does not yet mean firmware initialization or GPU compute works.

### C. Firmware and device lifecycle

- Implement the minimal GB10 lifecycle and required GSP firmware transport using inspectable, version-pinned interface sources. List exact firmware/protocol dependencies and known unknowns.
- Required vendor-signed device firmware is permitted by the governing architecture. Validate identity/integrity and compatibility before use; preserve source/notice provenance. No firmware-independence claim.
- Define ordered initialization, bounded waits, error states and recoverable shutdown. Document reset/power boundaries and device-wide effects.
- Prove initialization from a documented power/reset state without an earlier Linux GPU-driver initialization. A warm handoff from a Linux-initialized GPU is only a separately labelled intermediate result.
- If protocol information or initialization support is missing, record the precise blocker; do not substitute success-shaped stubs or inferred PASS.

### D. Native memory, queue and first compute

- Implement GPU address-space/page-table and shared-memory management separately from CPU MMU and SMMU services. Unified physical memory does not imply identical virtual addresses or automatic cache visibility.
- Bound and account for allocations; support cleanup after known completion. The existing bump DMA pool cannot silently stand in for a reusable allocator.
- Establish channel/GPFIFO, launch descriptors, doorbell and completion handling. Reuse Omega code/QMD builders only after validating context-dependent assumptions.
- Preserve shader-cache invalidation, output visibility, ordering and completion protections from the inspected session. A marker alone is not proof of correct output.
- A timeout after submission means uncertain completion: retain/quarantine resources and reject further work until an explicitly verified quiescence/recovery transition. Do not free memory still reachable by the GPU, erase the failure latch, or retry blindly.
- Run one existing Omega-generated integer vector-add program with varying inputs and CPU-checked expected results. Poison outputs with values guaranteed to differ from expectations; compare every output. Include partial-block and nontrivial sizes within documented bounds.
- Demonstrate normal teardown/reopen and repeated runs with bounded memory; unauthorized, revoked and stale requests must be refused before device effects.

### E. Follow-on, separately tracked

After first compute is proven, link bounded work for persistent sessions, matrix/attention kernels, model loading and end-to-end native inference/recovery. This issue is not closed by a plan alone, and it does not require implementing the entire CUDA ecosystem. Retiring the Linux driver for **normal AIEN operation** requires those follow-on workloads to pass too.

## Acceptance and evidence

- [ ] Inventory and ownership map; active lanes and execution-order blockers explicitly linked.
- [ ] Existing backend interface reused/extended; Linux behavior preserved; native target links without RM/UVM device-file access, Linux syscall/runtime requirements or CUDA userspace libraries.
- [ ] Multi-segment, read-only discovery tests pass; deliberate config-write mutation fails.
- [ ] Capability, MMIO, DMA translation and interrupt/polling limits tested; unknown topology and insufficient rights fail closed.
- [ ] Firmware/lifecycle protocols, blobs, versions and initialization state recorded; native initialization proved on physical GB10.
- [ ] Exact Omega-generated kernel executes under AIENOS after firmware handoff, with no Linux kernel/compatibility VM providing GPU service.
- [ ] All outputs match the CPU oracle; stale completion/unwritten output/incorrect result negative cases fail.
- [ ] Repeated success, known-completion cleanup and uncertain-completion quarantine tested; reset recovery claimed only when actually demonstrated.
- [ ] #285 satisfied in the same cut if domain-1 resource-number reuse or persistence is introduced.
- [ ] Receipts bind exact repository/dependency commits, toolchain and image digests, firmware identity, generated code, inputs/outputs, machine identity, commands, raw logs and environment.
- [ ] Host, simulated-device, QEMU, Linux-hosted GB10 and native physical GB10 results remain separate. QEMU without a real GB10 cannot qualify GSP/compute. Missing/skipped work is NOT_RUN or a named blocker, never PASS.
- [ ] Independent code/evidence review and current docs; historical receipts remain unchanged.

Initial work can proceed with host fixtures and builds. Physical experiments use the existing attended hardware, quiet-window, recovery and authorization procedures. This issue does not authorize deleting the Linux installation or removing the known-good recovery path.

## First implementation PR

Start with **the dependency map plus multi-segment non-mutating PCI discovery**, or extend the active PCI lane if it already owns that change. Include the fake-config test proving that discovery never invokes BAR sizing or writes configuration space, and a fixture locating the recorded GB10 identity on a nonzero segment. In parallel only where existing coordination permits, prepare the backend seam using the existing Omega engine contract. Do not begin with a model run or an unreviewed port of the entire NVIDIA Linux driver.

Parent: aien-dev/aien-architecture#190 (release readiness) · package **P09** · gate **N5** ("the question-and-answer flow runs on the GPU within its limits"). Owner: **unassigned until N4** (filed by worker w-scope, orchestrator job 12928250). Independent verifier: the orchestrator.

This is the bounded **delivery** issue for one frozen model answering through the native GB10 path on AIENOS. #286 stops at first compute (one checked integer vector calculation); #34 owns native **CPU** inference. Neither covers a model on the native GPU. This issue does not start before N3 and N4 are met, and it authorizes no hardware action by itself.

## Ground truth inventory (read-only, 2026-10-12)

Snapshots: aienos `ff5da2d`, omega `4d0bb36`, aien-sovereign-core `35e2910`. No builds or runs were done for this issue.

### What the native AIENOS session actually loads today (CPU, P06 cut 1 #312)

| Item | Fact | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model file | One pinned file: `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`, sha256 `3f5a2242...62dcc1`, 807,694,368 bytes | `crates/aienos-infer/tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md:4`, `docs/ATTENDED_SESSION_N1.md:63,156` |
| Container | GGUF v3, bounded reader, hostile input gives an error not a panic | `crates/aienos-infer/src/lib.rs:11-17`, `src/gguf.rs:416` |
| Architecture | Llama only: `llama_params()` refuses any `general.architecture` other than `llama` | `crates/aienos-infer/src/gguf.rs:549-551` |
| Weight types | Quantized: Q4_K and Q6_K only; plain floats F32, F16, BF16 (tried first per row); every other type refused with `QuantError::Unsupported`. The pinned file uses Q4_K and Q6_K | `src/model.rs:89-94`, `src/quant.rs:107,126-145`, `src/gguf.rs:619-635` |
| Operations | RMSNorm, Q/K/V, RoPE with llama3 per-pair factors, causal grouped-query attention, output projection, SwiGLU, greedy argmax; one token at a time | `src/decode.rs:1-7`, `src/model.rs:144-149` |
| Numerical precision | Scalar f32 compute, f32 KV cache, weights dequantized per row on the fly | `src/decode.rs:3,16-33` |
| Tokenizer | Llama-3 byte-level BPE built from the GGUF `tokenizer.ggml.*` arrays, `llama-bpe` pre-tokenizer, no regex engine | `src/tokenizer.rs:1-9` |
| Chat template | Hard-coded Llama-3 instruct one-user-turn template; stop token `<|eot_id|>` = 128009 | `src/tokenizer.rs:320-327`, `crates/aienos-infer-kernel/src/lib.rs:46` |
| Memory limits | 256 MiB bump heap for the Rust unit; model bytes in their own kernel frames; session limits: 64-position KV cache, 16 new tokens, 256-byte prompt, 64 KiB heap reserve; every frame returned at close (checked) | `native/kernel/core/infer.c:84,238-241,307,530,346-348` |
| Loading path | UEFI stub reads `\EFI\AIENOS\MODEL.MAP` (4096 bytes, GPT disk GUID, up to 128 LBA extents, declared SHA-256) and reads the model through firmware Block I/O before ExitBootServices; kernel recomputes SHA-256 and refuses to decode on mismatch. fw_cfg is TEST-ONLY (QEMU) | `native/boot/model_map.h:1-50`, `native/boot/efi_model.c:15,96`, `native/kernel/core/infer.c:573`, staging in #309 (`6a1ec34`), package manifests in #322 (`4958cbd`) |
| Production combination | Still refused: the inference probe library cannot be combined with hardware staging; the service image has no inference yet (that is N3 / #34) | `native/kernel/Makefile:264-266`, `docs/ATTENDED_SESSION_N1.md:95-110` |
| Emulator evidence | Golden prompt through the step API after a cancel: 17 prefill + 8 tokens, reply "The capital of France is Paris.", ids equal llama.cpp; 40.7 s per token under QEMU TCG (meaningless as speed) | `native/kernel/GATES.md` row 139d |

### What the hosted (Linux) GPU path uses

| Item | Fact | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Qwen3 family (Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507) from Safetensors checkpoints | `crates/aien-inference-abi/src/checkpoint.rs:1-2`, `fixtures/chat-templates/qwen3-*` |
| Precision | BF16 weights only (any other dtype is `DtypeMismatch`); FP32 decoded on demand | `checkpoint.rs:2,20-21` |
| Tokenizer and template | Qwen3 Jinja chat templates with render oracles | `crates/aien-inference-abi/fixtures/chat-templates/` |
| GPU kernels | Omega BF16 matmul and attention; no Q4_K or GGUF code in omega `src/` | `omega src/omega_gpu_matmul_api.c`, `src/omega_gpu_attention_api.h`; `git grep -i "q4_k\|gguf" src` returns nothing |
| Device access | Linux NVIDIA RM/UVM through `nvrm_open` | `omega src/omega_gpu_session.c:159` |

**Plain statement:** the hosted Qwen3 Safetensors/BF16 support does **not** imply native support for Llama/GGUF on the GPU, and it is **not** a portable native model runtime. The native side has a CPU Llama/GGUF path; the GPU side has BF16 Qwen3 kernels that reach the chip only through Linux. There is no shared model format, tokenizer, chat template or precision between them today, and no native GPU memory manager, queue or completion path (that is #286 cuts B-E).

## Scope (one frozen model, one native GPU path)

1. **Choose and freeze one model** and record the choice with its sha256 in this issue before code. The choice must say which of these it is and why: (a) the already pinned Llama-3.2-1B Q4_K_M GGUF, with its weights expanded to BF16 at load so the existing BF16 kernel family applies (needs a native expansion step and enough GPU-visible memory, roughly 2.5 GB, UNVERIFIED until measured); or (b) a BF16 Safetensors model, which needs a native Safetensors reader plus that model's tokenizer and template in the freestanding build. Both are new work; neither exists natively today.
2. **Correctness:** the native GPU reply for the golden prompt matches a recorded reference (token ids, or the stated tolerance on logits) from the same frozen file; the CPU native path (#34) stays the reference oracle.
3. **Performance:** report prefill time, per-token time and outputs per second on the native path, measured on the same prompt set as the reference; no target is claimed until measured.
4. **Cancellation:** a cancel between steps stops GPU work, leaves no queued work, and the next request answers correctly (same contract as P06 `session.rs` cancel).
5. **Persistence:** the approved answer and one remembered fact survive a restart through the sealed Store (same flow as N3), with the GPU path producing the answer.
6. **Backend evidence:** every run records which backend produced each step. **Intentional CPU placement** (an op the plan puts on the CPU, listed up front) is recorded as such; any **fallback** (GPU work that silently ran on the CPU or a Linux backend) fails the run.
7. **Within limits:** explicit caps on GPU memory, context positions, new tokens and prompt bytes, with refusals tested; every GPU and CPU resource is returned at close.

## Exclusions (separate issues, separate qualification)

Quantized GPU kernels (Q4_K/int8 on the GPU), speculative decoding, persistent or fused mega-kernels, multi-model serving, multi-user scheduling, broad CUDA compatibility, and any speed campaign. Hosted speed work stays in omega#328 and aien-sovereign-core#384.

## Dependencies

- **N3 = #34**: production service image with the model from the boot disk and the sealed Store together (lifts the refusal at `native/kernel/Makefile:264-266`), two-boot emulator proof.
- **N4 = #286**: native first compute (firmware load, channel, one checked vector calculation, clean quiesce). Physical, attended.
- **omega D/E boundary work**: omega#416 (cut A freestanding link target, merged `d708443c`) and its follow-ups that make the persistent inference session (`omega_gpu_session.c`) run on the native platform contract without pthreads, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` or nvrm.
- #285 resource incarnation counter if any domain-1 kernel resource number is reused.

## Acceptance (all measurable)

- [ ] Frozen model recorded (name, sha256, format, precision) and loaded through `MODEL.MAP`; hash mismatch refuses to decode.
- [ ] Emulator: everything that does not need the GPU (load, tokenizer, template, CPU-placed ops, refusals) passes in QEMU with receipts.
- [ ] Physical, attended: golden prompt answered on the native GPU path, ids/tolerance match the recorded reference, backend ledger shows zero fallback.
- [ ] Cancel mid-reply, then a correct reply; restart, the approved answer and one fact are still there.
- [ ] Resource accounting at close equals the count before open (GPU memory, frames, queues).
- [ ] Numbers recorded: prefill time, per-token time, outputs per second, peak GPU memory.

## Negative controls (each must FAIL or refuse as stated)

- Model file with one flipped byte: SHA-256 refusal, no decode.
- A model of the other architecture or an unsupported weight type: refused at load, not run.
- GPU path disabled or GPU init failing: the run is reported FAIL (or explicit CPU-only mode), never a silent CPU answer counted as GPU.
- Prompt over the byte cap, request over the position cap: refused.
- Cancel with nothing running: refused cleanly; second open while open: refused.

## Evidence ledger

| Item | Built | Emulator | Physical |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native CPU Llama/GGUF session (#34, P06) | yes | QEMU PASS (row 139d) | NOT_RUN |
| Production service image with model (N3) | no | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN |
| Native first compute (N4, #286) | groundwork only | no GPU simulator | NOT_RUN |
| Native GPU model path (this issue, N5) | no | NOT_RUN | NOT_RUN |

title: E03: Plan reuse campaign on the existing rx_plan cache
body:
Part of the necessary-work programme (epic: "Necessary-work programme: make the necessary work the limiting factor"). Plan section 6, row E03, priority P0. Status: NOT_RUN. Docs: [plan](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv/blob/research/necessary-work-program/docs/plans/necessary-work/AIEN_Physical_Limits_Project_Plan.md), [feasibility research](https://github.com/aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv/blob/research/necessary-work-program/docs/research/necessary-work-program-feasibility.md).

**In plain words:** Existing plan reuse removes repeated search with lower total cost.

**Hypothesis and predicted observation.** Existing plan reuse removes repeated search with lower total cost.

**Discriminating experiment and controls.** Cold solve, warm same instance, new bindings, changed preconditions; compare against the existing rx_plan baseline (tests/runtime/rx_plan_reuse.c); count retrieval and validation.

**Decision / deliverable.** Held-out reuse benefit and invalidation coverage; no general-agent claim from a toy domain.

**Depends on.** Phase 0.

**Who does it.** Plan role code: AGENT. Opus 5.5 builds (Astra for a targeted bug); Fable 5.1 reviews; Haiku 5.5 watches long runs.

**Gates before promotion** (plan section 9): G0 reproducible baseline (pins, hashes, device state), G1 trustworthy measurement, G2 correctness including mutants, G3 detectable benefit with predeclared effect size and repetitions, G4 full cost including search and fallback, G5 causal out-of-sample prediction, G6 independent reproduction. A faster incorrect candidate is a failed experiment.

**Reporting rule.** Seconds and joules per accepted objective and watts, each beside its physical bound with derivation and calc id, the same figure from our previous run, and the distance to the ceiling. Tokens and bytes are supporting facts only. Track C reports Turing yield T and T/J once TY-x exists; until then the acceptance-gate figure alone, labelled. No outside comparisons, no durations, no percent targets. Joules are UNMEASURED until an on-board or wall-meter instrument is named.

**Evidence.** One append-only campaign folder (omega-mv evidence/<CAMPAIGN>/README.md or sovereign-core-mv docs/inference/evidence/<campaign>/) using the plan section 10 fields plus claim_strength (proven_in_scope, measured, inferred, unresolved). GPU runs: quietlock check first, never killed, Spark judges, results land through the PR desk.


## Hardware-first learning extension (2026-10-19)
Requested by Drake; coordinated by #276, consumed by aien-dev/omega-mv#584. This extends this existing campaign; it does not commission a second plan cache or change the existing gates.

### Additional experiment: does retained experience repay its full cost?
- Use existing rx_plan paths. Measure cold acquisition, lookup hits/misses, applicability checks, execution, validation, failed reuse/repair, state storage/reload and maintenance. Keep seconds and joules separate; joules remain UNMEASURED without an instrument.
- Evaluate repeated tasks, held-out bindings/compositions, interference, changed preconditions, stale generations and restart. Freeze horizons and quality floors before evaluation. Compare no reuse, existing reuse and the proposed learning arm on the same task stream.
- A simple diagnostic model is net(H)=p*Delta*(1-r^H)/(1-r)-C for 0<r<1: C is one-time acquisition cost, p applicability probability, Delta net saving per applicable retained use, r per-opportunity retention, H opportunities. For r=1 use H*p*Delta-C; handle r=0 separately. With positive C,p,Delta and 0<r<1, C>=p*Delta/(1-r) means no finite positive payoff. Derive assumptions/units and verify against a direct finite sum using aien-calc receipts. Maintenance and nonstationary streams need explicit extra terms or direct accounting.
- Estimate p/r/Delta from development observations, then predict held-out cumulative cost; never assume constant exponential capability growth. Report sensitivity and model failure. The geometric equation is a diagnostic approximation, not a law of intelligence.
- Distinguish time/energy saved from savings reinvested in more learning; report the reinvestment ledger without counting the same benefit twice. Include forgetting, negative transfer and memory growth.

### Additional acceptance
- [ ] Full lifecycle ledger reconciles with traces, including failed acquisition/reuse.
- [ ] Positive-payoff and no-payoff controls detect the expected sign; stale/corrupt plans refuse or revalidate through existing rules.
- [ ] Predicted and measured break-even horizons plus uncertainty are reported on held-out streams under #262.
- [ ] Retention/transfer/restart outcomes and quality floors are reported alongside cost; no general-agent claim from blocks-world alone.
- [ ] Preserve prior gates and historical failures; append immutable new evidence and independent review. #276 tracks Symposium crossover before overlapping runtime changes.


## Minimum-work policy integration (2026-10-19)
Parent #276 now requires one persistent entity with a view projected from committed state. Reuse artifacts must remain bound to the existing persistent identity, semantic assumptions and generations across view detachment/reconnection and restart; this does not change Cortex or generation-store ownership.

Add ablations for existing reuse alone versus #249's checked elimination, incremental update and combined behavior through omega-mv#584. Include invalidation, lookup misses and maintenance. Stop acquiring/maintaining a shortcut when the declared policy predicts no net payoff within the frozen horizon; evaluate that policy against a bounded always-search control. Report saved resources separately from resources reinvested in further learning. Existing gates and historical evidence are unchanged.

title: Hardware-first learning research: simulate costs, search bounded mechanisms, measure compounding (extends #265)
body:
## Purpose
Drake requests mathematical simulation before expensive compute: model the Spark, compare bounded candidate learning mechanisms, and measure whether retained experience compounds useful capability per second and joule. A conversational interface is required eventually; an LLM architecture is not assumed. This issue coordinates only the additional research slice under the existing necessary-work programme #265; it does not replace that programme or reorder the active execution plan.

## Current-code audit, 2026-10-19
Read current default-branch source through GitHub:
- omega-mv src/runtime/rx_costmodel.c already fits empirical costs, handles uncertainty/pressure, observes failures and estimates energy when power inputs exist. Reuse it; do not recreate a learned estimator.
- omega-mv src/runtime/rx_plan.c already encodes templates, checks applicability and executes verified reuse. Extend the existing E03 campaign (#246), not a new cache.
- omega-mv src/omega_realize_synth.c already emits bound native realizations; its schedule choice is a bounded issue-width/register heuristic. This is not an unrestricted intelligence synthesizer.
- GPU simulator work is active (omega-mv PRs #514 and #509); simulator correctness cannot establish timing/energy or chip correctness for unverified instructions.
- FORM0 exists (physics-mv PR #46; architecture PR #127). Respect physical-form identity and reuse its accepted contract where applicable.
These are source observations and PR descriptions, not rerun qualification. Implementers must pin fresh commits and inspect tests/build contracts before changes.

## Reuse and dependencies
Use #264 objective contracts, #244 real traces, #246 reuse campaign, #252 timer calibration, #253 hardware atlas, #262 out-of-sample predictions and #263 final dossier. Coordinate with #274 FORTRAN scarcity work (lifetimes, frequency, resident layouts, storage maps). GPU variant ranking remains omega-mv#522. Byte translation validation and bounded rewrites remain #248/#249/#261. Existing ALLEN work (#159/#231/#269) owns communication and continuity.

## Symposium crossover: unresolved
Requested explicitly by Drake. Searches for symposium/sympos in accessible aien-dev code, issues, PRs and commits, plus aien-spark/drakestapleton issues and installed repository names, did not identify the intended project. This is not evidence of absence. Before allocating overlapping implementation, record the intended Symposium repository/branch, inspect its actual source and open PRs, and mark each proposed deliverable reuse/extend/missing. Do not assume an unrelated public project named Symposium is the intended one. Independent offline contract work may proceed; overlapping runtime changes wait for this check.

## Scope and gates
1. Freeze a finite task suite and budgets using existing Phase 0. Include task success, delayed retention, transfer, correction handling, communication cost and recovery; choose numerical thresholds before held-out evaluation.
2. Add an offline resource-DAG simulator consuming existing measured evidence; distinguish spec ceilings, fitted estimates, measured values and unknowns. Use it to reject infeasible candidates and nominate informative small measurements.
3. Add a bounded candidate-search experiment over representations/update rules/realizations. Existing generation stores and verification execute accepted candidates. No unrestricted self-modification or new compiler/runtime.
4. Extend E03 with lifecycle payback/retention accounting. Savings reinvested in learning are not simultaneously counted as energy saved.
5. Publish a Pareto set in seconds and joules per accepted objective, peak bytes, quality/retention/transfer, and T/T-per-J where the existing TY protocol applies. Include search, failed trials, validation, persistence and interface costs. Whole-system energy stays UNMEASURED without a named instrument. No global optimum or general intelligence claim.

## Ownership and sequence
Coordinator owns only this ledger and contract reconciliation. Simulator owner owns additive offline harness; search owner owns bounded candidate experiment; E03 owner retains reuse campaign. Freeze shared evidence schema first; then use existing calibration/trace producers; then held-out validation; only then a small native pilot and existing release qualification. Runtime path changes require owning-workstream coordination.

## Completion
- [ ] Existing-code/PR/Symposium overlap matrix and pinned source links recorded.
- [ ] Child interfaces, budgets and held-out gates frozen before experiments.
- [ ] Simulator prediction error and selection regret measured on unseen cases under #262.
- [ ] Lifecycle learning payoff reported, including failures and no-payoff regimes.
- [ ] Native pilot uses existing execution/persistence with qualified fallback and no authority bypass.
- [ ] #263 receives a reproducible dossier and explicitly bounded verdict.

## Child ledger
- [ ] aien-dev/omega-mv#583 — offline resource-DAG simulator and held-out cost validation.
- [ ] aien-dev/omega-mv#584 — bounded learning search and native pilot (depends on #583).
- [ ] #246 — reused E03 campaign, extended with lifecycle payback, retention and reinvestment accounting.

Start with overlap/contract reconciliation, then #583; #246 can collect baseline observations within its existing scope. #584 consumes both. No experiment has run as part of this filing.


## Delivery rules
Status: PROPOSED. Qualification: NOT_RUN. This is a finite workstream, NOT A MASTER PLAN. Follow PLAN_AUTHORITY.md, CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md, accepted ADRs and the owning repository's AGENTS.md. Recheck current source and active PRs before coding; claim one owner/worktree per path. Preserve existing World, Cortex, FORGE, AEGIS and capability ownership. No new runtime authority or parallel cost-model service. Use existing native toolchain and aien-calc receipts; no Python/CUDA runtime dependency. Spark judges; quietlock check before GPU work; never kill chip runs; submit through the existing PR desk. Record pinned commits, commands, immutable evidence and independent review. Report PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/NOT_RUN separately from task completion; negative findings are valid outcomes. No performance or intelligence claim from a simulation alone.


## Operator clarification: one entity, minimum necessary computation (2026-10-19)
Drake's clarified product intent: one persistent, agent-first entity whose goals, memory, learning, machine actions and human-facing display form a coherent experience. The display is a projection of its state; closing a view must not erase or stop independently authorized work. An LLM may help build it and is not required as its permanent engine. “One entity” does not require one binary or removal of internal isolation/capability boundaries. Preserve existing subsystem ownership; any actual boundary change follows the accepted ADR process.

The objective is to eliminate as much unnecessary computation as possible, not promise zero processing. For each accepted objective: (1) prove work unnecessary or derive a direct result, (2) reuse a verified result under valid assumptions, (3) update only changed dependencies, (4) simplify remaining work and movement, (5) optimize only when expected lifecycle benefit pays for search/check/storage/maintenance. Hard correctness, authority, recovery and declared capability floors remain constraints.

### Formal contract
Let s be persistent entity state, e an admitted event, and theta the versioned learned mechanisms. Define s_next=F_theta(s,e) and a view v=R(s,h), where h is the human's view/interaction context. These are specifications to map onto existing World/ALLEN/Cortex/AIENOS mechanisms, not a new event loop or store. Input effects, rendering and state transitions still require physical work. A view update must not independently mutate authoritative state outside the existing command/commit path.

For a frozen workload W and horizon H, minimize the Pareto pair (total seconds, total joules) subject to success, retention, transfer, response, rights and recovery gates. Count offline construction/search, validation, failed attempts, actual execution, persistence and presentation. Never hide a transferred cost or trade lower quality for an apparent saving.

### Assigned extensions and acceptance
- [ ] #249 owns assumption-checked mathematical elimination and hardware-cost ranking; omega-mv#583 models their full cost; omega-mv#584 executes the bounded integration.
- [ ] Existing ALLEN interface/continuity owners (#159/#231/#269) coordinate the entity/view demonstration through omega-mv#584; no duplicate UI/kernel/model project.
- [ ] One objective continues with the view detached; reattachment shows the same committed identity/state/history. A human correction enters the same authoritative state; restart preserves it.
- [ ] An unchanged-state interval performs no avoidable repeated inference/search or application-level redraw. Report required timers, IO and display scanout separately; never claim zero hardware activity.
- [ ] A changed input recomputes exactly the dependency closure needed by the contract; stale cache/state mutations force invalidation.
- [ ] Retained experience makes a declared repeated workload cheaper after all costs, or record FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE. Report unknown coverage rather than claiming all possible work has been eliminated.
- [ ] Add an ablation ladder: incumbent; elimination only; reuse only; incremental update only; combined; include optimization overhead and stop-search control. Use #263 for final evidence.

title: Offline resource-DAG cost simulation using existing cost model and measured Spark traces
body:
Parent: aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#276. New scope is offline composition of existing measurements, not replacement of rx_costmodel or GPU simulators.

## Current state and dependencies
Current default-branch src/runtime/rx_costmodel.c already models operation costs with uncertainty; src/omega_realize_synth.c already emits native bytes using a bounded schedule heuristic. tests/bw_warp_sim* are correctness models with active work in PRs #514/#509; do not treat them as calibrated timing models. Consume architecture #244 traces, #252 clocks, #253 hardware atlas and #274 lifetime/storage-map work; use #262 held-out prediction gate and #263 dossier. GPU variant-selection adapter belongs to #522. Reconcile Symposium crossover under parent before overlapping runtime changes.

## Implement
1. Freeze a versioned offline schema: machine/build/calibration identities, units, validity envelope, provenance (specified/measured/fitted/synthetic/unknown), operation DAG, resource demands, shared-memory traffic, buffer lifetimes, dependencies and completion/synchronization events. Unknown fields remain unknown. CPU and GPU unified memory share one capacity ledger.
2. Build a deterministic finite resource-DAG evaluator. Model CPU/GPU compute, DRAM bandwidth contention, cache/residency where supported by evidence, launches, barriers, storage IO and persistent-state updates. Begin with the smallest trace-backed subset; explicitly refuse unsupported paths. Reuse rx_costmodel for learned operation estimates; this harness only composes costs and constraints.
3. Document bounds with assumptions. For one operation, max(F/P,Q/B) is an ideal compute/traffic overlap floor; additive launch cost is valid only when serialized. Whole-DAG critical path and resource-work bounds must both hold. No sum of concurrent full-bandwidth claims; no sparse FP4 headline as dense training throughput.
4. Account for whole-system energy using a named instrument and integration boundary E=integral P(t)dt. Device-only observations stay device-only. TDP is not measured wall power. - [ ] Reproducible CLI example consumes a pinned trace and emits machine-readable costs, bounds, provenance and a Pareto table. No GPU execution in offline mode.
- [ ] Independent reviewer reproduces results; chip measurements use existing apparatus. Unsupported coverage and failed hypotheses appear in the dossier.

## Ownership and closure
One owner for additive offline harness/schema/tests. Coordinate changes to rx_costmodel with its owner; do not edit GPU encoders/driver/runtime scheduling in this issue. PRs reference this issue and pin upstream evidence. Deliver source, schema, commands, frozen fixtures, predictions and receipts; completion can record a falsified cost hypothesis.

Report PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/NOT_RUN separately from task completion; negative findings are valid outcomes. No performance or intelligence claim from a simulation alone.


## Minimum-work accounting extension (parent clarification 2026-10-19)
Represent baseline and transformed DAGs with stable operation/dependency IDs. For each removed operation record the valid derivation, reused-result identity or unchanged-dependency condition that permits removal. Derive break-even regions symbolically where tractable and validate with direct sums and measured samples. If uncertainty obscures net benefit, return INCONCLUSIVE rather than promote. All existing gates remain in force.

title: Bounded learning-mechanism search: simulation screening, native pilot, retention and lifecycle payoff
body:
Parent: aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#276. Depends on #583 for cost screening and architecture #264/#246/#262 for objective, reuse and validation contracts.

## Goal and current state
Test whether a finite search over learning mechanisms can find a better lifecycle tradeoff on one Spark than the declared incumbent. Do not assume an LLM or promise general intelligence. Define state z, action a=pi_theta(z,x), update z_next=U_theta(z,x,a,feedback). Theta ranges over an explicitly enumerated finite grammar, not all possible intelligences. First experiment compares: (A) fixed/no-learning incumbent; (B) existing verified plan retrieval/reuse; (C) one bounded incremental rule learner or compact predictor whose supported operations already lower through Omega. Freeze grammar, numeric domains, state capacity, maximum steps/search candidates, update frequency, random seeds, evaluation protocol and fallback. Add architectures only through a separately recorded scope amendment.

## Work
1. Specify the same finite tasks for all arms: repeated objectives, novel bindings/compositions, delayed recall after interference, changed rules and correction handling. Use existing Phase 0 suite where applicable. Split search/training, calibration and sealed evaluation; do not select on the sealed set.
2. Include a costed communication adapter through existing ALLEN interface ownership; start with bounded textual commands plus clarification/abstention checks. Do not equate this with open-domain conversation. If an existing model is used for language, charge its full cost and report its contribution separately.
3. Offline search uses #583 to reject infeasible memory/compute/traffic proposals and shortlist candidates. Optimize a Pareto frontier of lifecycle seconds, joules (only when instrumented) and peak bytes subject to frozen success/retention/transfer/recovery constraints. Include search, failed candidates, compilation, verification, updates, retrieval misses, repair, persistence and interface costs. No weighted score that hides a violated quality constraint.
4. Execute only a bounded pilot through existing semantic contracts, realizations and capability checks. Persist candidate state/rules as versioned, digest-bound artifacts through the owning generation/store protocol. Do not write an independent disk image/store or bypass Cortex promotion. Verify restart and OLD-or-NEW recovery.
5. Fit learning/retention expectations from observations. Cost equations alone cannot predict capability. Select further measurements only within the frozen budget; record when uncertainty prevents choosing a winner.

## Acceptance and scientific controls
- [ ] Candidate grammar and exact supported lowering coverage published; unknown operations rejected before execution.
- [ ] Baselines use matched task exposure and declared lifecycle budgets; all failed searches count. Include shuffled feedback, disabled learning, stale/wrong memory and unseen-composition controls.
- [ ] Semantic correctness (including mutants) is evaluated separately from empirical usefulness. Sampled differential tests are labelled sampled, not proof.
- [ ] A stored candidate reloads with bound identities, passes recovery/refusal checks and falls back safely on corrupt/stale state.
- [ ] Precommit meaningful quality floors and retention intervals before the sealed evaluation; publish all arms and failures with uncertainty and #262 prediction results.
- [ ] Report break-even horizon and no-payoff regions using the E03 extension. A faster lookup on one toy task is not evidence of general transfer or accelerating intelligence.
- [ ] Independent reviewer reproduces one candidate and baseline from pinned artifacts; dossier goes to architecture #263. PASS means the bounded hypothesis passed, not an industry-wide breakthrough.

title: Bounded exploration across temporary regressions: preserve incumbent and test delayed payoff
body:
## Purpose
Drake clarified the governing principle: “Only spend computation when it improves the outcome,” with an essential caveat: a temporarily worse change may enable a much better subsequent change that greedy selection would never discover.

Operational proposal: improve outcomes over a declared horizon while reserving bounded resources for exploration whose value is uncertain. Preserve the best qualified incumbent; exploratory states need not improve monotonically. No policy can guarantee discovery of every beneficial continuation.

Status: PROPOSED. Qualification: NOT_RUN. No experiment or performance claim accompanies this filing.

## Relationship to existing work — extend, do not duplicate
- Parent: aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#276, within its existing necessary-work programme.
- #584 already owns finite learning-mechanism search, persistence, native pilot and lifecycle evaluation. This issue specifies a discriminating experiment within that workstream, not another search engine.
- #583 owns offline cost composition and uncertainty; reuse its estimates and accounting.
- aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#249 owns checked rewrite search and equivalence. It already compares greedy and bounded equality exploration; keep rewrite implementation there.
- aien-dev/aien-architecture-mv#246 retains reuse/retention/payback ownership; #262/#263 in that repository own prediction gates and evidence.

Clarification to #584’s stopping paragraph: retaining the incumbent is a deployment decision, not a requirement to discard every uncertain or temporarily inferior research branch. An estimated negative immediate gain is not by itself a proof that every continuation is unprofitable. Any production-policy change must be reviewed under the existing owning plan.

## Current source anchor and audit boundary
Current indexed Omega source at a8ffd2b912c84197d08f963b05f9c7d8b30a3f8a exposes omega_synth_equiv_contains_or_add in src/omega_synthesis.c and ranks signatures using instruction-count costs in tools/omegatool.c. Source:
https://github.com/aien-dev/omega-mv/blob/a8ffd2b912c84197d08f963b05f9c7d8b30a3f8a/src/omega_synthesis.c

This does not establish that the whole project lacks exploration or that its current pruning is incorrect. Recheck current source, tests, open PRs, plan authority and Symposium overlap before implementation. Map each deliverable to existing ownership; use additive experiment paths first.

## Hypothesis
At the same total lifecycle budget, retaining selected temporarily inferior candidates can discover qualified improvements missed by immediate-improvement-only search. Added search/storage/checking costs may erase the advantage: FAIL and INCONCLUSIVE are valid findings.

## Freeze the experiment before evaluation
1. Use a finite candidate grammar and transition relation supported by #584/#249. Declare whether a branch changes a learning mechanism or a semantics-preserving implementation; do not conflate those experiments.
2. Freeze workloads, quality/correctness floors, objective horizon, seeds, candidate/depth limits, retained-branch capacity, checkpoint/storage limits, and total search/check/execution budgets. Specify exploration allocation and continuation/stop rules before sealed evaluation; no arbitrary universal exploration percentage.
3. Compare: A immediate-improvement-only search; B the existing bounded search where available; C bounded search retaining some inferior intermediate states; D a matched-budget random-search control where feasible. Match task exposure and charge all failed trials.
4. Build a small finite landscape with a documented cost valley: a beneficial terminal candidate requires an initially worse transition under the declared grammar. Enumerate the small fixture to establish reachability and optimum only within that fixture. Include monotone and no-payoff fixtures so C is not rewarded only on a constructed favorable example.
5. Evaluate separately on held-out task families not used to tune the valley or policy. A synthetic valley demonstrates a mechanism, not real-world capability or a hardware speedup.

## Required behavior
- Keep an immutable reference to the qualified incumbent and isolate candidate state through existing generation/Cortex mechanisms. No new store, scheduler, authority or unapproved effects.
- Branch identity binds parent, candidate artifact, semantic/learning contract, assumptions, exposure history, measurements and consumed budget.
- A candidate may regress on optimization metrics or empirical development performance inside the isolated experiment. Correctness/authority checks remain hard gates for execution and promotion. No invalid rewrite becomes acceptable because it might lead somewhere useful; symbolic intermediates must remain well-defined and checked under #249.
- Predeclare how branches receive another bounded tranche: observed progress, uncertainty, diversity or a small explicitly budgeted exploratory allocation. An information-value claim requires a declared downstream decision and calibration; “curiosity” cannot justify unbounded work.
- Stops distinguish exhausted budget, invalid candidate, measured poor payoff and unresolved potential. Budget exhaustion is not proof of futility.
- Promotion requires existing correctness, quality, retention, recovery and independent-review gates. A temporarily worse research branch never silently replaces the working entity.
- Retain useful negative findings only with scope/provenance and storage/lookup/expiry cost. Do not generalize one failed branch into a universal impossibility claim.

## Acceptance and reporting
- [ ] Existing implementation/PR overlap map and pinned source recorded; no duplicate optimizer.
- [ ] Valley fixture shows greedy A misses a reachable better candidate and C can reach it within its declared budget; negative fixtures and all failures published.
- [ ] Matched-budget held-out comparison reports accepted outcomes, total seconds, peak bytes, search/check/storage/recovery overhead and uncertainty; joules remain UNMEASURED without a named instrument. Do not hide quality violations in a weighted score.
- [ ] Report best-qualified result versus cumulative budget, branch abandonment, false pruning and selection regret where a finite reference permits calculation. Do not claim a global optimum outside enumerated scope.
- [ ] Budget accounting includes unsuccessful branches, failed verification, candidate evaluation, persistence, invalidation, fallback and any language/interface cost.
- [ ] Restart reconstructs incumbent/candidate identities and consumed budget without duplicate promotion or effects; corrupt/stale candidates are refused.
- [ ] Deployment incumbent remains intact after a failed experiment; final candidate passes existing gates before promotion.
- [ ] Deliver reproducible commands, frozen fixtures, branch traces, cost receipts and an independent review to the parent dossier. Report whether exploration repaid its cost over the declared horizon, including no-payoff regions.

## Delivery
One experiment owner coordinated with #584 and #249 owners. Follow current PLAN_AUTHORITY.md, CURRENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md, accepted ADRs and AGENTS.md; this issue does not reorder the active plan. Use the existing native toolchain and aien-calc/evidence conventions. Offline fixtures first; native Spark work only through existing qualification and quietlock/PR-desk procedures; never interrupt chip runs. Simulation alone cannot establish physical energy savings or intelligence gains.
